## §0 GLOBAL NON-NEGOTIABLE SYSTEM INVARIANTS

### §0.1 Inherited Sprint 1–5 Invariants (ALL ACTIVE — ZERO EXCEPTIONS)

Sprint 6 code that violates ANY of these is categorically invalid regardless of functional correctness.

| ID | Invariant | Violation Signal |
|---|---|---|
| INV-1 | DB `$transaction` is the ONLY correctness authority | Any business-critical multi-write outside `$transaction` |
| INV-2 | Inventory quantity NEVER goes negative | `quantity - delta < 0` passes without rejection |
| INV-3 | Atomic mutation bundle: quantity + movement + reservation + EventOutbox | Any of these four written in separate operations |
| INV-4 | Lock acquired BEFORE transaction, released AFTER commit | `reserve()` called inside `$transaction` |
| INV-5 | Optimistic locking `version` check mandatory on inventory mutations | `update` without `version` match |
| INV-6 | Idempotency key is the FIRST operation | Any DB write before idempotency check |
| INV-7 | `InventoryMovement` is APPEND-ONLY — forever | Any `update()` or `delete()` on InventoryMovement |
| INV-8 | Redis is display optimization ONLY — never correctness authority | Redis miss causing 500 or data loss |
| INV-9 | Server-computed timestamps — never client-provided | Any timestamp field set from request body |
| INV-10 | Zero-oversell — enforced at DB layer | Stock going negative under concurrent load |
| INV-13 | `OrderStatusHistory` is APPEND-ONLY — forever | Any `update()` or `delete()` on OrderStatusHistory |
| INV-17 | EventOutbox dedup keys are deterministic | `Date.now()`, `randomUUID()` in dedup key |
| INV-20 | `eventVersion` + `schemaVersion` on EVERY EventOutbox record | EventOutbox.create() missing either field |
| INV-S5-1 | `Order.sellerId` is `Business.id`, NEVER `User.id` | Comparing sellerId to req.user.id directly |
| INV-S5-2 | `SellerContextGuard` on EVERY `/seller/*` route | Absent guard on any seller controller |
| INV-S5-4 | Seller NEVER receives `order.buyerId`, `buyer.phone`, or `buyer.email` | Raw buyerId in seller-facing payload |
| INV-S5-8 | Every seller status transition atomically writes order + history + outbox | Separate writes outside `$transaction` |

### §0.2 Sprint 6 New Invariants

| ID | Invariant | Enforcement Layer |
|---|---|---|
| **INV-S6-1** | `NotificationModule` is a PURE CONSUMER — it NEVER writes to `EventOutbox`, NEVER imports `OrderService`, `InventoryService`, `PaymentService`, `SellerOrderService`, or `BuyerOrderService` | Module boundary + import audit |
| **INV-S6-2** | `OutboxConsumerWorker` marks EventOutbox `status = COMPLETED` ONLY AFTER successful BullMQ enqueue. If enqueue fails, event stays PENDING. | Worker implementation order |
| **INV-S6-3** | ALL EventOutbox payload reads MUST use `safeParse()` (not `parse()`) with the appropriate Zod schema from `@vyaparnet/types`. Invalid payloads: log + mark FAILED + skip. Worker MUST NOT crash. | `OutboxConsumerWorker` boundary |
| **INV-S6-4** | Every `Notification` record in DB MUST have `userId` populated. ALL `NotificationRepository` methods accept `userId` as mandatory first parameter and filter by it. | Repository method signatures |
| **INV-S6-5** | `NotificationPreference` check is the FIRST operation in every channel delivery path. No SMS/Email/Push is sent before preference is verified. | `NotificationWorker` delivery pipeline |
| **INV-S6-6** | Notification deduplication Redis key MUST be deterministic: `notif:{userId}:{eventType}:{entityId}`. TTL = 300s. NEVER use `Date.now()` or `randomUUID()` in dedup key. | `DeduplicationService` |
| **INV-S6-7** | Buyer's phone number, email, and full name MUST NOT appear in seller-directed notifications or seller-accessible notification records. `buyerCode` masking from Sprint 5 extends to notification layer. | Template rendering + seller notification DTO |
| **INV-S6-8** | Each delivery channel is an INDEPENDENT BullMQ job. SMS failure MUST NOT block Email delivery. Email failure MUST NOT block Push delivery. Any single channel failure is isolated. | Job design in `OutboxConsumerWorker` |
| **INV-S6-9** | `PushSubscription` table: one row per `(userId, endpoint)` unique pair. On `410 Gone` from push service: delete subscription immediately (sync, not async). NEVER accumulate stale subscriptions. | `WebPushService` + PushSubscription repository |
| **INV-S6-10** | `SupplierScoreUpdated` notifications are sent ONLY when `Math.abs(compositeScore - previousCompositeScore) >= 5`. The EventOutbox source threshold (>=1 point) is UNCHANGED from Sprint 5. This filter lives in `NotificationWorker`. | `handleSupplierScoreUpdated()` handler |
| **INV-S6-11** | Low-stock notifications: maximum 1 SMS per `(productId, businessId)` per 24 hours. Redis key: `notif:lowstock:{productId}:{businessId}` TTL=86400s. Checked BEFORE enqueuing SMS job. | `handleStockLow()` handler |
| **INV-S6-12** | `OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP` is an extensible registry (Record<string, EventHandler>) — NOT a switch/case. Sprint 7/8 adds handlers by adding entries to this map. | `OutboxConsumerWorker` routing |
| **INV-S6-13** | `NotificationModule` MUST NOT consume `OrderConfirmed` or `OrderCancelled` Sprint 4 legacy events. ONLY `OrderStatusChanged` governs order lifecycle notifications. Consuming both causes guaranteed duplicate notifications. | `OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP` entries |
| **INV-S6-14** | Template rendering MUST use safe string substitution ONLY. No `eval()`, no template literal injection. All substituted values are sanitized (strip HTML, strip SMS-dangerous chars, max 200 chars). | `TemplateService.render()` |
| **INV-S6-15** | `UserContactService` is notification-module-local. It queries `User` table directly via Prisma (read-only). It MUST NOT import `UsersModule` or `UsersService`. | Module boundary |
| **INV-S6-16** | `NotificationWorker` verifies phone/email non-null BEFORE attempting delivery. Null phone/email = skip + warn log. Never pass null to SMS/Email provider — provider may throw unhandled exception. | Channel delivery methods |
| **INV-S6-17** | EventOutbox idempotency: Redis key `outbox-processed:{eventId}` TTL=86400s. Check BEFORE processing in `OutboxConsumerWorker`. If key exists: mark COMPLETED (idempotent), skip BullMQ enqueue. | `OutboxConsumerWorker` |
| **INV-S6-18** | `GET /notifications` and `GET /notifications/unread-count` MUST include `userId = req.user.id` in EVERY DB query. Cross-user notification access is a P0 security violation. | `NotificationController` + `NotificationRepository` |
| **INV-S6-19** | `schemaVersion: '6.0'` and `eventVersion: '1.0'` on ALL Sprint 6 EventOutbox writes. Sprint 6 writes 0 EventOutbox events — this invariant is a guard against future agent adding outbox writes without version. | Audit gate |
| **INV-S6-20** | In-App notification creation is SYNCHRONOUS (direct DB write, not via BullMQ). It is the channel of last resort — it must be created even if all external channels fail. | `NotificationWorker.createInAppNotification()` |
| **INV-S6-21** | Channel Circuit Breaker MUST be applied to SMS and Email channels. If 5 consecutive failures occur within a 60s window, the circuit OPENS for 120s. During open circuit: skip delivery, log `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN`, do NOT enqueue retry. Push is best-effort and exempt. | `SmsChannel.send()`, `EmailChannel.send()`, `CircuitBreakerService` |
| **INV-S6-22** | `PushSubscription` records per user are CAPPED at 10 active subscriptions. On subscribe when cap is reached: delete oldest `createdAt` subscription before inserting new one. Prevents amplification attacks. | `PushSubscriptionRepository.upsert()` |
| **INV-S6-23** | Email HTML template variables (`title`, `body`, CTA text) MUST be HTML-entity-escaped before injection into HTML string. `&` → `&amp;`, `<` → `&lt;`, `>` → `&gt;`, `"` → `&quot;`. The `TemplateService.sanitize()` handles SMS/plain-text; a separate `htmlEscape()` function handles email HTML context. | `EmailChannel.buildEmailHtml()` |
| **INV-S6-24** | Notification list cursor is the notification `id` (CUID) — NOT `createdAt`. CUIDs are monotonically sortable and unique. `createdAt`-based cursors are non-unique and MUST NOT be used. | `NotificationRepository.findManyForUser()` |
| **INV-S6-25** | `handleOrderCreated` MUST set a seller-specific dedup key SEPARATELY from the buyer dedup key. Format: `notif:{sellerUserId}:OrderCreated:{orderId}`. Absence of this key means the seller receives duplicate notifications on event replay. | `order-created.handler.ts` |
| **INV-S6-26** | `OutboxConsumerWorker` cron MUST be guarded against overlap: if previous poll is still running when next cron fires, skip the new cycle. Use an in-memory `isPolling` boolean flag (not Redis — single-process guard is sufficient). | `OutboxConsumerWorker.pollEventOutbox()` |
| **INV-S6-27** | `validatePayload()` MUST return `{ success: false }` for unknown event types — NOT `{ success: true, data: payload }`. Unknown event types have no schema and no handler and MUST be marked `COMPLETED` with a `warn` log. A pass-through creates an unsanitized data path. | `OutboxConsumerWorker.validatePayload()` |
| **INV-S6-28** | `NotificationTemplate` seed MUST NOT update `bodyHi`, `bodyEn`, `titleHi`, `titleEn` on startup if the template is `isActive = true`. Template body updates are a deploy-time decision, not a startup side-effect. Seed uses `create` only with `upsert` that has EMPTY `update: {}` for body fields (only `isActive` updated). Exception: `isActive` field may be toggled. | `TemplateSeedService.seedTemplates()` |
| **INV-S6-29** | `DELETE /notifications/push/unsubscribe` request body MUST be validated with a Zod schema (`PushUnsubscribeSchema: { endpoint: z.string().url() }`) before processing. Unvalidated body allows null/undefined endpoint to propagate to repository delete. | `NotificationController.unsubscribe()` |
| **INV-S6-30** | `notificationMonth` partition key MUST be computed in UTC: `format(new Date(), 'yyyy-MM', { timeZone: 'UTC' })`. Server timezone drift creates incorrect partition keys causing cross-month index failures. | `NotificationRepository.create()` |

## §2 SPRINT 5 INHERITANCE CONTRACT

Sprint 6 inherits all Sprint 5 guarantees without exception:

| Guarantee | Sprint 5 Deliverable | Sprint 6 Consumes |
|---|---|---|
| `OrderStatusChanged` events | All seller transitions + buyer cancellation | Primary notification trigger |
| `SupplierScoreUpdated` events | 6-hour cron, ≥1 point change threshold | Score change notifications (≥5 pt filter added by Sprint 6) |
| `orderStatusHistory.actorRole` | SELLER/BUYER/SYSTEM attribution | Notification body: "Seller ne ship kiya" vs "Aapne cancel kiya" |
| `OrderTracking.dispatchProofUrl` | Optional S3 URL | Not used in Sprint 6 notifications (Sprint 8 dispute context) |
| `SellerScore` table | Current + previous composite score | `SupplierScoreUpdated` payload carries both values |
| `EventOutbox.schemaVersion = '5.0'` | All Sprint 5 events | `OutboxConsumerWorker` validates this on parse |
| `EventOutbox.estimatedDelivery` | Added in Sprint 5 R1 fix | `OrderStatusChanged` SHIPPED payload includes it |
| `outbox-payloads.schemas.ts` | Created in Sprint 5 R2 | Sprint 6 imports these schemas for payload validation |

### §2.1 Sprint 5 Events Available for Consumption

| EventType | Source | schemaVersion | Payload Schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OrderCreated` | `orders.service.ts` (Sprint 4) | `4.3` | `OrderCreatedPayloadSchema` (to be created in Sprint 6 Phase 1) |
| `OrderStatusChanged` | `seller-order.service.ts`, `buyer-order.service.ts` | `5.0` | `OrderStatusChangedPayloadSchema` (in `outbox-payloads.schemas.ts`) |
| `PaymentReceived` | `orders.service.ts` (Sprint 4 COD) | `4.3` | `PaymentReceivedPayloadSchema` (to be created in Sprint 6 Phase 1) |
| `PaymentFailed` | `payment.service.ts` (Sprint 4) | `4.3` | `PaymentFailedPayloadSchema` (to be created in Sprint 6 Phase 1) |
| `SupplierScoreUpdated` | `seller-scorecard.service.ts` | `5.0` | `SupplierScoreUpdatedPayloadSchema` (in `outbox-payloads.schemas.ts`) |
| `StockLow` | `inventory.service.ts` (Sprint 3) | `3.0` | `StockLowPayloadSchema` (to be created in Sprint 6 Phase 1) |

> **CRITICAL:** Do NOT consume `OrderConfirmed` or `OrderCancelled` (Sprint 4 legacy events). Use ONLY `OrderStatusChanged` for order lifecycle. See INV-S6-13.

## §3 SCHEMA CHANGES & MIGRATIONS

### §3.1 Models Already in Schema v4.3 (Activation Only — No Schema Change)

```prisma
model Notification {
  id                String               @id @default(cuid())
  userId            String
  type              NotificationType
  title             String
  body              String
  channels          NotificationChannel[]
  metadata          Json?
  isRead            Boolean              @default(false)
  readAt            DateTime?
  createdAt         DateTime             @default(now())
  isDeleted         Boolean              @default(false)
  notificationMonth String               // Partition key
  user              User                 @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  @@index([userId, isRead, createdAt], map: "idx_notif_user_read_date")
}

model NotificationTemplate {
  id        String               @id @default(cuid())
  name      String               @unique
  type      NotificationType
  channels  NotificationChannel[]
  titleHi   String
  bodyHi    String
  titleEn   String
  bodyEn    String
  isActive  Boolean              @default(true)
  createdAt DateTime             @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime             @updatedAt
}
```

**Enums already in schema:**
```prisma
enum NotificationType { ORDER PAYMENT INVENTORY MARKETING SYSTEM KYC RETURN DISPUTE PROMOTION }
enum NotificationChannel { PUSH SMS WHATSAPP EMAIL IN_APP }
```

### §3.2 New Model: PushSubscription (Sprint 6 Migration Required)

**Decision D2.7a:** Multi-device support requires separate table. One user can have multiple subscribed devices.

```prisma
model PushSubscription {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  endpoint  String
  p256dh    String   // Encryption key
  auth      String   // Auth secret
  userAgent String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
  isActive  Boolean  @default(true)

  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  @@unique([userId, endpoint], map: "uq_push_sub_user_endpoint")
  @@index([userId, isActive], map: "idx_push_sub_user_active")
}
```

**User model relation to add:**
```prisma
// In User model, add:
pushSubscriptions PushSubscription[]
```

### §3.3 Migration Strategy

```
Migration name: 20260601_sprint6_push_subscription_and_notification_activation
Steps:
  1. CREATE TABLE "PushSubscription" (as above)
  2. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "uq_push_sub_user_endpoint"
  3. CREATE INDEX "idx_push_sub_user_active"
  4. Verify "Notification" and "NotificationTemplate" tables exist (from v4.3)
  5. Verify "idx_notif_user_read_date" index exists
  6. No destructive changes — additive only
```

### §3.4 Notification Seed Data

`NotificationTemplate` seed must run at app startup (idempotent — use `upsert`). All templates must exist before any notification can be sent.

**Template naming convention:** `{EventType}_{Role}_{Lang}` — e.g., `OrderCreated_BUYER_hi`

| Template Name | Type | Channels | titleHi | bodyHi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OrderCreated_BUYER_hi` | ORDER | SMS, IN_APP, EMAIL | `Order place ho gaya!` | `Aapka order #{orderNumber} place ho gaya hai. Amount: {grandTotal}` |
| `OrderCreated_SELLER_hi` | ORDER | SMS, IN_APP, EMAIL | `Naya order aaya!` | `Order #{orderNumber} aaya hai. Amount: {grandTotal}. Abhi confirm karein.` |
| `OrderConfirmed_BUYER_hi` | ORDER | SMS, IN_APP | `Order confirm ho gaya!` | `#{orderNumber} - Seller ne aapka order accept kar liya!` |
| `OrderProcessing_BUYER_hi` | ORDER | IN_APP | `Order pack ho raha hai` | `#{orderNumber} - Aapka order pack ho raha hai.` |
| `OrderShipped_BUYER_hi` | ORDER | SMS, IN_APP | `Order ship ho gaya!` | `#{orderNumber} ship ho gaya! Tracking: {trackingNumber}` |
| `PaymentReceived_BUYER_hi` | PAYMENT | SMS, IN_APP, EMAIL | `Payment successful!` | `#{orderNumber} ke liye {grandTotal} ka payment receive ho gaya.` |
| `PaymentFailed_BUYER_hi` | PAYMENT | SMS, IN_APP, EMAIL | `Payment fail ho gayi` | `#{orderNumber} ka payment fail ho gaya. Retry karein.` |
| `ScoreImproved_SELLER_hi` | SYSTEM | IN_APP | `Score badh gaya!` | `Aapka supplier score {compositeScore} ho gaya! Pehle {previousCompositeScore} tha.` |
| `ScoreDropped_SELLER_hi` | SYSTEM | SMS, IN_APP | `Score gir gaya` | `Aapka score {previousCompositeScore} se {compositeScore} ho gaya. Improvement karein!` |
| `StockLow_SELLER_hi` | INVENTORY | SMS, IN_APP | `Stock kam ho raha hai` | `{productName} ka stock sirf {stockQty} reh gaya hai. Update karein.` |
| `OrderCreated_BUYER_en` | ORDER | SMS, IN_APP, EMAIL | `Order Placed!` | `Your order #{orderNumber} has been placed. Amount: {grandTotal}` |
| `OrderShipped_BUYER_en` | ORDER | SMS, IN_APP | `Order Shipped!` | `#{orderNumber} has been shipped! Tracking: {trackingNumber}` |
| `PaymentFailed_BUYER_en` | PAYMENT | SMS, IN_APP, EMAIL | `Payment Failed` | `Payment for #{orderNumber} failed. Please retry.` |

> All remaining English templates follow same pattern. Minimum set: all Hindi templates required for MVP. English templates required for all SMS/EMAIL events.

## §4 REDIS KEY REGISTRY

Sprint 6 adds these Redis keys. All existing Sprint 1–5 keys unchanged.

| Key Pattern | TTL | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notif:{userId}:{eventType}:{entityId}` | 300s | Notification deduplication per event per user | `DeduplicationService` |
| `notif:lowstock:{productId}:{businessId}` | 86400s | Low-stock rate limit (1/day per product per seller) | `handleStockLow()` handler |
| `outbox-processed:{eventId}` | 86400s | EventOutbox event idempotency | `OutboxConsumerWorker` |
| `outbox-consumer-lock:{eventId}` | 30s | Prevents concurrent worker processing same event | `OutboxConsumerWorker` |
| `notif:pref:{userId}` | 300s | Cached notification preferences | `NotificationPreferenceService` |
| `notif:unread-count:{userId}` | 30s | Cached unread notification count | `NotificationRepository` |
| `cb:sms:failures` | 60s (sliding window) | SMS circuit breaker failure counter (INV-S6-21) | `CircuitBreakerService` |
| `cb:sms:open` | 120s | SMS circuit breaker open state (INV-S6-21) | `CircuitBreakerService` |
| `cb:email:failures` | 60s (sliding window) | Email circuit breaker failure counter (INV-S6-21) | `CircuitBreakerService` |
| `cb:email:open` | 120s | Email circuit breaker open state (INV-S6-21) | `CircuitBreakerService` |

> **Redis Key Namespace Rules (Hardened):**
> - All Sprint 6 keys use lowercase prefix with colon separators: `notif:`, `outbox-`, `cb:`
> - `notif:{userId}:{eventType}:{entityId}` — `eventType` MUST use the exact `EventOutbox.eventType` string (e.g., `OrderCreated`, `OrderStatusChanged_CONFIRMED`). No abbreviation.
> - `cb:` keys are per-channel (`sms`, `email`), NOT per-user. Circuit breaker is a platform-wide provider health signal.
> - No Sprint 6 key uses `Date.now()` or `randomUUID()` as part of the key.

**Redis failure mode (ALL keys):** On Redis error — log warning, continue operation. Redis failure MUST NOT block notification creation (In-App) or preference lookup (use DB fallback).

**Circuit Breaker Redis failure mode:** If Redis is unavailable during circuit breaker check — assume circuit is CLOSED (allow delivery attempt). Log `CB_REDIS_UNAVAILABLE`. Do NOT assume circuit is OPEN on Redis failure — this would block all delivery.

**Redis is NEVER the source of truth.** DB is authority for all notification state.

## §5 BULLMQ QUEUE ARCHITECTURE

### §5.1 Queue Registration (Already Exists)

`notifications` queue already registered in `BullMQModule` (Sprint 0). Sprint 6 adds workers only.

### §5.2 New Workers

| Worker | Queue | Concurrency | Schedule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OutboxConsumerWorker` | Internal (polls DB) | 1 instance | Every 5s cron |
| `NotificationWorker` | `notifications` | 10 concurrent | Event-driven |

### §5.3 Job Schema

```typescript
interface NotificationJob {
  channel: 'sms' | 'email' | 'push';
  userId: string;
  notificationId: string;   // DB Notification record ID
  templateName: string;
  variables: Record<string, string>;
  // Resolved at enqueue time — no extra DB lookups per job retry
  title: string;            // Pre-rendered title (from TemplateService)
  body: string;             // Pre-rendered body (from TemplateService)
  eventType: string;        // For metrics labels (e.g. 'OrderCreated', 'OrderStatusChanged')
  segment?: string;         // For metrics labels — sourced from event payload if present
  // Channel-specific
  phone?: string;           // Pre-resolved at enqueue time (SMS)
  email?: string;           // Pre-resolved at enqueue time (Email)
  // Push: no endpoint — WebPushService queries all active subscriptions for userId
}
```

> **AF-2 Audit Fix:** `title`, `body`, `eventType`, and `segment` added to `NotificationJob`. These are referenced throughout worker code (`job.data.eventType`, `job.body`, `job.data.title`) but were absent from the interface definition. `title`+`body` are pre-rendered at enqueue time so each retry does not re-render. `eventType` + `segment` are required for Prometheus metric labels `notification_sent_total{channel, eventType, segment}` (§9.1).

**Why resolve contact at enqueue time?** Contact resolution (DB query) happens once in `OutboxConsumerWorker`. NotificationWorker receives ready-to-use contact info — no additional DB lookup needed per job retry.

### §5.4 Job Configuration

```typescript
// Default job options for notifications queue
{
  attempts: 3,
  backoff: { type: 'fixed', delay: 5000 },    // 5s, 10s, 20s for attempts 1,2,3
  removeOnComplete: { count: 1000, age: 24 * 3600 },
  removeOnFail: { count: 5000, age: 7 * 24 * 3600 },
  timeout: 30000,   // 30s per job (SMS/Email provider timeout)
}
```

**DLQ behavior:** After 3 failed attempts → job moves to `notifications-failed` queue. `NotificationsMetricsService` increments `notification_dlq_size` gauge.

### §5.5 OutboxConsumerWorker Scheduling

```typescript
// BullMQ RepeatableJob cron — runs every 5 seconds
@Cron('*/5 * * * * *') // every 5 seconds — NestJS @Cron decorator
async pollEventOutbox(): Promise<void> {
  // Process batch of 50 PENDING events
  // FIFO by createdAt
}
```

## §6 MODULE STRUCTURE & PACKAGE BOUNDARIES

### §6.1 New Module Structure

```
apps/api/src/modules/notification/
├── notification.module.ts
```

## §7 API CONTRACT REFERENCE

### §7.1 Notification Center APIs

| Method | Route | Auth | Role | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/notifications` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Paginated notification list (cursor-based) |
| PATCH | `/notifications/:id/read` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Mark single notification as read |
| PATCH | `/notifications/read-all` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Mark all unread as read |
| GET | `/notifications/unread-count` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Badge count (lightweight) |

### §7.2 Preference APIs

| Method | Route | Auth | Role | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/notifications/preferences` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Get current preferences |
| PUT | `/notifications/preferences` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Update preferences |

### §7.3 Push Subscription APIs

| Method | Route | Auth | Role | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/notifications/push/subscribe` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Register push subscription |
| DELETE | `/notifications/push/unsubscribe` | JWT | BUYER + SELLER | Remove push subscription |
| GET | `/notifications/push/vapid-public-key` | Public | Any | Frontend fetches VAPID public key |

### §7.4 API Response Envelope (Standard Platform Pattern)

```typescript
// GET /notifications
{
  success: true,
  data: {
    items: NotificationDto[],
    nextCursor: string | null,
    hasMore: boolean
  }
}

// GET /notifications/unread-count
{ success: true, data: { count: number } }

// GET /notifications/preferences
{ success: true, data: NotificationPreference }
```

### §7.5 Route Security

- NO `SellerContextGuard` on any notification route (INV-S6-18 — notifications are user-scoped, not business-scoped)
- Auth: `JwtAuthGuard` (global, inherited)
- Role: `@Roles(UserRole.BUYER, UserRole.SELLER)` on all notification routes
- Ownership: `userId = req.user.id` enforced at repository layer (INV-S6-18)

## §8 EVENTOUTBOX GOVERNANCE (SPRINT 6)

### §8.1 Sprint 6 EventOutbox Writes: ZERO

Sprint 6 produces ZERO EventOutbox events. All notification delivery is infrastructure — it has no domain state to announce. This is non-negotiable (INV-S6-1).

### §8.2 EventOutbox Read Governance

OutboxConsumerWorker reads EventOutbox with this exact query:

```typescript
const events = await prisma.eventOutbox.findMany({
  where: {
    status: 'PENDING',
    eventType: { in: Object.keys(OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP) },
  },
  orderBy: { createdAt: 'asc' },
  take: 50,
  select: {
    id: true,
    eventType: true,
    payload: true,
    schemaVersion: true,
    deduplicationKey: true,
    createdAt: true,
  },
});
```

**No SELECT FOR UPDATE.** Idempotency via Redis lock (INV-S6-17). This allows multiple worker instances without deadlocks.

### §8.3 EventOutbox Status Update Sequence (MANDATORY ORDER)

```typescript
// STEP 1: Acquire Redis lock (prevents concurrent processing)
const lockAcquired = await redis.set(
  `outbox-consumer-lock:${eventId}`, '1', 'NX', 'EX', 30
);
if (!lockAcquired) continue; // Another worker is processing this event

// STEP 2: Check idempotency key
const alreadyProcessed = await redis.exists(`outbox-processed:${eventId}`);
if (alreadyProcessed) {
  await prisma.eventOutbox.update({
    where: { id: eventId },
    data: { status: 'COMPLETED', processedAt: new Date() }
  });
  continue;
}

// STEP 3: Validate payload
const handler = OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP[event.eventType];
if (!handler) {
  this.logger.warn({ eventId, eventType }, 'OUTBOX_NO_HANDLER');
  await this.markEventCompleted(eventId); // No handler = complete without processing
  continue;
}

// STEP 4: Process (routes to handler → enqueues BullMQ jobs)
const result = await handler(event, this.context);

// STEP 5 — ONLY ON SUCCESS: Mark completed + set idempotency key
if (result.success) {
  await Promise.all([
    prisma.eventOutbox.update({
      where: { id: eventId },
      data: { status: 'COMPLETED', processedAt: new Date() }
    }),
    redis.set(`outbox-processed:${eventId}`, '1', 'EX', 86400),
  ]);
} else {
  await prisma.eventOutbox.update({
    where: { id: eventId },
    data: { status: 'FAILED', lastError: result.error }
  });
}
```

### §8.4 OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP Registry

```typescript

import { handleOrderCreated } from '../handlers/order-created.handler';
```

### §9.2 Alerts (Grafana)

|---|---|---|---|
| `notification_queue_depth > 5000` | For 5 minutes | WARNING | Ops: scale NotificationWorker instances |
| `notification_failed_total rate > 10%` | Over 5 min window, per channel | WARNING | Ops: check provider status |

### §9.3 Structured Logging (Mandatory Events)

```typescript
// On every notification sent (INFO)
this.logger.info({ userId, channel, eventType, notificationId }, 'NOTIFICATION_SENT');

// On dedup skip (INFO)
this.logger.info({ userId, eventType, entityId }, 'NOTIFICATION_DEDUP_SKIPPED');

// On invalid payload (ERROR)
this.logger.error({ eventId, eventType, errors }, 'OUTBOX_PAYLOAD_INVALID');

// On null phone/email skip (WARN)
this.logger.warn({ userId, channel }, 'NOTIFICATION_SKIPPED_NO_CONTACT');

// On preference skip (INFO)
this.logger.info({ userId, channel, eventType }, 'NOTIFICATION_PREF_SKIP');

// On DLQ (ERROR)
this.logger.error({ jobId, userId, channel, error }, 'NOTIFICATION_DLQ');

// On push 410 Gone (WARN)
this.logger.warn({ userId, endpoint }, 'PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION_DELETED_STALE');
```

**PII redaction rules (mandatory):**
- Phone: log last 4 digits only `****${phone.slice(-4)}`
- Email: log domain only `****@${email.split('@')[1]}`
- Name: log first name only
- NEVER log: full phone, full email, push endpoint URL

## §10 DEGRADED-MODE BEHAVIOR

### §10.1 Redis Unavailable

| Component | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `DeduplicationService` | Log warning, SKIP dedup check, proceed with send. Risk: possible duplicate. Acceptable for Redis failure scenario. |
| `NotificationPreferenceService` | Log warning, fall back to DB read. Never block notification on Redis failure. |
| `OutboxConsumerWorker` lock | Log warning, skip event in this cycle (retry next 5s). Do NOT process without lock during Redis outage. |
| `notif:unread-count` cache | Fall back to DB count. |

### §10.2 SMS Provider Unavailable

| Component | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `SmsChannel.send()` | Throw. BullMQ catches → retry 3x with backoff. After 3 failures → DLQ. |
| In-App notification | Created synchronously BEFORE SMS job is enqueued. SMS failure does NOT affect In-App. |
| Email delivery | Independent job — continues regardless of SMS failure. |

### §10.3 Email Provider Unavailable

Same pattern as SMS. Independent jobs. 3 retries → DLQ.

### §10.4 Push Service Unavailable

Push is best-effort. 1 retry. After failure → skip (no DLQ for push). Log warning.

Rationale: Push delivery is browser-dependent. Provider outage = acceptable loss for push.

### §10.5 OutboxConsumerWorker Failure

EventOutbox events remain in `PENDING` state. On worker restart, they will be re-processed (idempotency via `outbox-processed:{eventId}` key prevents duplicate delivery). No data loss.

---

## §10.6 CHANNEL CIRCUIT BREAKER ARCHITECTURE (INV-S6-21)

**Rationale:** SMS and Email providers (MSG91, Resend) can experience transient or sustained outages. Without circuit breakers, a provider outage causes every notification job to fail, retry 3x, and flood the DLQ. At scale (1000 sellers x high order volume), this creates a retry storm cascading into BullMQ queue pressure, increased Redis load, and wasted provider API quota. Circuit breakers isolate provider failure from the notification system.

**Push is exempt** — push is best-effort, already silenced at provider error, no DLQ.

### §10.6.1 Circuit Breaker State Machine

```
CLOSED (normal) --[ 5 failures in 60s ]--> OPEN (no delivery, 120s)
    ^                                              |
    +------------ HALF-OPEN <--[ 120s elapsed ]----+
              [ 1 success ] -----------------------> CLOSED
              [ 1 failure ] -----------------------> OPEN (reset 120s)
```

### §10.6.2 CircuitBreakerService Implementation Contract

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/services/circuit-breaker.service.ts
@Injectable()
export class CircuitBreakerService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(CircuitBreakerService.name);
  constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {}

  // Returns true if circuit is OPEN (do NOT deliver)
  async isOpen(channel: 'sms' | 'email'): Promise<boolean> {
    try {
      const open = await this.redis.exists(`cb:${channel}:open`);
      return open === 1;
    } catch {
      // INV-S6-21: Redis unavailable = assume CLOSED. NEVER assume OPEN on Redis failure.
      this.logger.warn({ channel }, 'CB_REDIS_UNAVAILABLE_ASSUME_CLOSED');
      return false;
    }
  }

  // Called on EACH delivery failure
  async recordFailure(channel: 'sms' | 'email'): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const key = `cb:${channel}:failures`;
      const count = await this.redis.incr(key);
      if (count === 1) await this.redis.expire(key, 60); // 60s sliding window
      if (count >= 5) {
        await this.redis.set(`cb:${channel}:open`, '1', 'EX', 120);
        this.logger.warn({ channel, failureCount: count }, 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPENED');
      }
    } catch { /* Redis failure: swallow */ }
  }

  // Called on EACH delivery success
  async recordSuccess(channel: 'sms' | 'email'): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.redis.del(`cb:${channel}:failures`, `cb:${channel}:open`);
    } catch { /* swallow */ }
  }
}
```

### §10.6.3 Channel Integration Pattern (SMS — Email follows same pattern)

```typescript
// In SmsChannel.send() — BEFORE any delivery attempt:
if (await this.circuitBreakerService.isOpen('sms')) {
  this.logger.warn({ userId: job.userId }, 'CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN_SMS_SKIPPED');
  this.metrics.notificationFailedTotal.inc({ channel: 'sms', reason: 'circuit_open', eventType: job.eventType ?? 'unknown' });
  return; // Do NOT throw. Do NOT trigger retry. Silent skip.
}
try {
  const result = await this.smsService.sendTransactional(job.phone!, job.body!);
  if (!result.success) {
    await this.circuitBreakerService.recordFailure('sms');
    throw new Error(`SMS delivery failed: ${result.error}`);
  }
  await this.circuitBreakerService.recordSuccess('sms');
} catch (err) {
  await this.circuitBreakerService.recordFailure('sms');
  throw err; // Re-throw for BullMQ retry
}
```

### §10.6.4 Circuit Breaker Observability Additions

Add to `metrics.providers.ts`:[
```typescript
makeGaugeProvider({ name: 'cb_state', help: 'Circuit breaker state (1=open,0=closed)', labelNames: ['channel'] }),
makeCounterProvider({ name: 'cb_skipped_total', help: 'Deliveries skipped due to open circuit', labelNames: ['channel'] }),
```

Grafana Alert: `cb_state{channel="sms"} == 1 for 2 minutes` → WARNING: Check MSG91 status.

### §10.6.5 Circuit Breaker Validation Gate

```
✅ 5 consecutive SMS failures in 60s → circuit opens
✅ 6th SMS during open circuit → SKIPPED (no throw, no retry enqueued)
✅ CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPENED log appears with channel + failureCount
✅ cb_skipped_total increments on each skipped delivery
✅ 120s elapsed → circuit auto-closes → delivery resumes
✅ 1 success during half-open → circuit resets to CLOSED
✅ Redis unavailable → isOpen() returns false → delivery proceeds
```

```typescript
@Injectable()
export class NotificationRepository {
  constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) {}

  // INV-S6-4 + INV-S6-30: userId MANDATORY, notificationMonth computed in UTC
  async create(userId: string, data: CreateNotificationData): Promise<{ id: string }> {
    // INV-S6-30: UTC partition key — prevents timezone drift creating wrong monthly buckets
    const notificationMonth = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7); // 'YYYY-MM' in UTC
    return this.prisma.notification.create({
      data: {
        userId,                       // INV-S6-4
        type: data.type,
        title: data.title,
        body: data.body,
        channels: data.channels,
        metadata: data.metadata ?? null,
        notificationMonth,
        isRead: false,
      },
      select: { id: true },
    });
  }

  // INV-S6-18: userId filter MANDATORY. INV-S6-24: Cursor uses notification `id` (CUID) NOT createdAt.
  async findManyForUser(
    userId: string,
    query: NotificationListQuery,
  ): Promise<{ items: NotificationDto[]; nextCursor: string | null; hasMore: boolean }> {
    const limit = query.limit ?? 20;
    const rows = await this.prisma.notification.findMany({
      where: {
        userId,            // INV-S6-18
        isDeleted: false,
        ...(query.isRead !== undefined && { isRead: query.isRead }),
        // INV-S6-24: cursor is notification `id` (CUID) — CUIDs are monotonically sortable
        // NOT createdAt — createdAt timestamps are non-unique at millisecond precision
        ...(query.cursor && { id: { lt: query.cursor } }),
      },
      orderBy: { id: 'desc' }, // Sort by CUID (monotonic), not createdAt
      take: limit + 1,
      select: {
        id: true, type: true, title: true, body: true,
        isRead: true, readAt: true, createdAt: true, metadata: true,
      },
    });

    const hasMore = rows.length > limit;
    const items = hasMore ? rows.slice(0, limit) : rows;
    // INV-S6-24: nextCursor is the last item's `id` (CUID), not createdAt
    const nextCursor = hasMore ? items[items.length - 1].id : null;

    return {
      items: items.map(this.toDto),
      nextCursor,
      hasMore,
    };
  }

  // INV-S6-18: Ownership check before mark-read
  async markRead(notificationId: string, userId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.prisma.notification.updateMany({
      where: { id: notificationId, userId },  // userId MANDATORY — prevents cross-user mark
      data: { isRead: true, readAt: new Date() },
    });
  }

  async markAllRead(userId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.prisma.notification.updateMany({
      where: { userId, isRead: false, isDeleted: false },
      data: { isRead: true, readAt: new Date() },
    });
  }

  // Unread count — capped at 100 to prevent full table scan
  async countUnread(userId: string): Promise<number> {
    const result = await this.prisma.notification.count({
      where: { userId, isRead: false, isDeleted: false },
    });
    return Math.min(result, 100); // Cap at 100 for badge display
  }

  private toDto(row: RawNotificationRow): NotificationDto {
    return {
      id: row.id,
      type: row.type,
      title: row.title,
      body: row.body,
      isRead: row.isRead,
      readAt: row.readAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString(),
      metadata: row.metadata as Record<string, string> | null,
    };
  }
}
```

### §13.3 NotificationTemplate Seed

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/services/template-seed.service.ts
@Injectable()
export class TemplateSeedService implements OnModuleInit {
  constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) {}

  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.seedTemplates();
  }

  private async seedTemplates(): Promise<void> {
    const templates = this.getTemplateDefinitions();
    // INV-S6-28: Idempotent create-only upsert.
    // `update: {}` is intentionally empty for body/title fields.
    // Template content changes are deploy decisions, NOT startup side-effects.
    // Only `isActive` is allowed to be toggled by seed on subsequent startups.
    for (const template of templates) {
      await this.prisma.notificationTemplate.upsert({
        where: { name: template.name },
        update: { isActive: template.isActive }, // INV-S6-28: Only toggle isActive, never overwrite body
        create: template,
      });
    }
  }

  private getTemplateDefinitions() {
    return [
      {
        name: 'OrderCreated_BUYER_hi',
        type: NotificationType.ORDER,
        channels: [NotificationChannel.SMS, NotificationChannel.IN_APP, NotificationChannel.EMAIL],
        titleHi: 'Order place ho gaya!',
        bodyHi: 'Aapka order #{{orderNumber}} place ho gaya hai. Amount: ₹{{grandTotal}}',
        titleEn: 'Order Placed!',
        bodyEn: 'Your order #{{orderNumber}} has been placed. Amount: ₹{{grandTotal}}',
        isActive: true,
      },
      // ... all other templates from §3.4
    ];
  }
}
```

### §13.4 Phase 2 Validation Gate

```
✅ pnpm --filter database prisma migrate status → all migrations applied
✅ PushSubscription table exists with correct columns and indexes
✅ Notification table accessible from NotificationRepository
✅ NotificationTemplate seed runs on app startup (check logs)
✅ All 11+ templates seeded in DB
✅ pnpm --filter api build → 0 errors after module scaffold
```

**AI Footguns — Phase 2:**
```
FOOTGUN-2-A: Forgetting to add PushSubscription relation to User model in schema.prisma.
Fix: User model must have "pushSubscriptions PushSubscription[]" relation.

FOOTGUN-2-B: Template seed using create() instead of upsert() — fails on second startup.
Fix: Always use upsert({ where: { name }, create, update }) for seed data.

FOOTGUN-2-C: NotificationRepository.markRead() using findUnique + update (2 queries) instead of updateMany with userId filter (1 atomic query).
Fix: updateMany({ where: { id, userId }, data: { isRead: true } }) — atomic and safe.

FOOTGUN-2-D: TemplateSeedService updating template bodyHi/bodyEn/titleHi/titleEn on every app startup. (Hardening v1.1)
Fix: INV-S6-28 — seed upsert MUST use empty update object for body fields: update: { isActive: template.isActive }.
Only isActive may be toggled. Silently overwriting production templates on restart corrupts live content.

FOOTGUN-2-E: NotificationRepository pagination cursor using createdAt timestamp. (Hardening v1.1)
Fix: INV-S6-24 — cursor MUST be notification `id` (CUID). CUIDs are monotonically sortable and globally unique.
createdAt is non-unique at millisecond resolution — two simultaneous notifications break cursor pagination.

FOOTGUN-2-F: notificationMonth computed using server local timezone (e.g. IST). (Hardening v1.1)
Fix: INV-S6-30 — use new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7). Always UTC. Never new Date() formatted with local timezone.
IST server at 00:01 computes '2026-06' but DB timestamps are '2026-05' in UTC — wrong monthly bucket.
```

## §14 PHASE 3 — EVENT CONSUMPTION ARCHITECTURE

**Objective:** OutboxConsumerWorker polls EventOutbox and routes events to handlers.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Pro (complex routing logic, idempotency critical)

### §14.1 Channel Abstraction Interface

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/channels/channel.interface.ts
export interface INotificationChannel {
  name: 'sms' | 'email' | 'push';
  send(job: NotificationJob): Promise<void>;
}
```

### §14.2 OutboxConsumerWorker

```typescript
@Injectable()
export class OutboxConsumerWorker {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(OutboxConsumerWorker.name);
  private isPolling = false; // INV-S6-26: Cron overlap guard

  constructor(
    private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
    private readonly redis: RedisService,
    @InjectQueue('notifications') private readonly notificationsQueue: Queue,
    private readonly notificationService: NotificationService,
    private readonly userContactService: UserContactService,
    private readonly deduplicationService: DeduplicationService,
    private readonly notificationPreferenceService: NotificationPreferenceService,
    private readonly metrics: NotificationMetricsService,
  ) {}

  // Run every 5 seconds
  @Cron(CronExpression.EVERY_5_SECONDS, { name: 'outbox-consumer-cron' })
  async pollEventOutbox(): Promise<void> {
    // INV-S6-26: Overlap guard — skip if previous poll still running
    if (this.isPolling) {
      this.logger.debug('OUTBOX_POLL_SKIPPED_OVERLAP');
      return;
    }
    this.isPolling = true;
    try {
      const events = await this.fetchPendingEvents();
      if (events.length === 0) return;

      this.logger.debug({ count: events.length }, 'OUTBOX_POLL_BATCH');

      for (const event of events) {
        await this.processEvent(event);
      }
    } finally {
      this.isPolling = false; // Always release — even on error
    }
  }

  private async processEvent(event: OutboxEventRow): Promise<void> {
    const { id: eventId, eventType } = event;

    // STEP 1: Acquire Redis lock (INV-S6-17)
    const lockAcquired = await this.redis.set(
      `outbox-consumer-lock:${eventId}`, '1', 'NX', 'EX', 30
    );
    if (!lockAcquired) {
      this.logger.debug({ eventId }, 'OUTBOX_LOCK_NOT_ACQUIRED');
      return;
    }

    try {
      // STEP 2: Idempotency check (INV-S6-17)
      const alreadyProcessed = await this.redis.exists(`outbox-processed:${eventId}`);
      if (alreadyProcessed) {
        await this.markEventCompleted(eventId);
        return;
      }

      // STEP 3: Get handler
      const handler = OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP[eventType];
      if (!handler) {
        this.logger.warn({ eventId, eventType }, 'OUTBOX_NO_HANDLER');
        await this.markEventCompleted(eventId);
        return;
      }

      // STEP 4: Validate payload (INV-S6-3)
      const payloadResult = this.validatePayload(eventType, event.payload);
      if (!payloadResult.success) {
        this.logger.error({ eventId, eventType, errors: payloadResult.error }, 'OUTBOX_PAYLOAD_INVALID');
        await this.markEventFailed(eventId, 'INVALID_PAYLOAD');
        this.metrics.notificationOutboxFailedTotal.inc({ reason: 'invalid_payload' });
        return;
      }

      // STEP 5: Route to handler
      await handler(payloadResult.data, this.buildContext());
      this.metrics.notificationOutboxConsumedTotal.inc({ eventType });

      // STEP 6 — ONLY AFTER SUCCESS: Mark completed (INV-S6-2)
      await Promise.all([
        this.markEventCompleted(eventId),
        this.redis.set(`outbox-processed:${eventId}`, '1', 'EX', 86400),
      ]);

    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.error({ eventId, eventType, error: (err as Error).message }, 'OUTBOX_PROCESS_ERROR');
      await this.markEventFailed(eventId, (err as Error).message);
    }
  }

  private validatePayload(eventType: string, payload: unknown): SafeParseReturnType<unknown, unknown> {
    const schemaMap: Record<string, z.ZodTypeAny> = {
      OrderCreated: OrderCreatedPayloadSchema,
      OrderStatusChanged: OrderStatusChangedPayloadSchema,
      PaymentReceived: PaymentReceivedPayloadSchema,
      PaymentFailed: PaymentFailedPayloadSchema,
      SupplierScoreUpdated: SupplierScoreUpdatedPayloadSchema,
      StockLow: StockLowPayloadSchema,
    };
    const schema = schemaMap[eventType];
    // INV-S6-27: Unknown event type = ALWAYS fail validation.
    // Handler check (STEP 3) already guards unknown eventTypes — they never reach STEP 4.
    // If somehow reached, return failure to prevent unsanitized payload propagation.
    if (!schema) {
      return { success: false, error: new z.ZodError([{ code: 'custom', path: [], message: `No schema for eventType: ${eventType}` }]) };
    }
    return schema.safeParse(payload);
  }

  private buildContext(): HandlerContext {
    return {
      notificationService: this.notificationService,
      userContactService: this.userContactService,
      deduplicationService: this.deduplicationService,
      preferenceService: this.notificationPreferenceService,
      notificationsQueue: this.notificationsQueue,
      metrics: this.metrics,
      logger: this.logger,
    };
  }

  private async fetchPendingEvents() {
    return this.prisma.eventOutbox.findMany({
      where: {
        status: 'PENDING',
        eventType: { in: Object.keys(OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP) },
      },
      orderBy: { createdAt: 'asc' },
      take: 50,
      select: { id: true, eventType: true, payload: true, schemaVersion: true, createdAt: true },
    });
  }

  private async markEventCompleted(eventId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.prisma.eventOutbox.update({
      where: { id: eventId },
      data: { status: 'COMPLETED', processedAt: new Date() },
    });
  }

  private async markEventFailed(eventId: string, error: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.prisma.eventOutbox.update({
      where: { id: eventId },
      data: { status: 'FAILED', lastError: error },
    });
  }
}
```

### §14.3 Handler Pattern

All handlers follow this exact pattern:

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/handlers/order-created.handler.ts
export async function handleOrderCreated(
  payload: OrderCreatedPayload,
  ctx: HandlerContext,
): Promise<void> {
  const { orderId, orderNumber, buyerId, sellerId, grandTotal, segment } = payload;

  // 1. Buyer dedup check (INV-S6-6)
  const dedupKeyBuyer = `notif:${buyerId}:OrderCreated:${orderId}`;
  if (await ctx.deduplicationService.isDuplicate(dedupKeyBuyer)) {
    ctx.logger.info({ buyerId, orderId }, 'NOTIFICATION_DEDUP_SKIPPED');
    ctx.metrics.notificationDedupSkippedTotal.inc({ eventType: 'OrderCreated' });
    return;
  }

  // 2. Resolve contacts
  const buyerContact = await ctx.userContactService.getContact(buyerId);
  const sellerUserId = await ctx.userContactService.getBusinessOwnerUserId(sellerId);
  const sellerContact = sellerUserId ? await ctx.userContactService.getContact(sellerUserId) : null;

  // 3. Build template variables
  const vars = { orderNumber, grandTotal };

  // 4. Buyer notifications
  await ctx.notificationService.createAndEnqueue({
    userId: buyerId,
    contact: buyerContact,
    templateName: 'OrderCreated_BUYER',
    variables: vars,
    entityId: orderId,
    eventType: 'OrderCreated',
    channels: ['sms', 'email', 'inApp'],
  });

  // 5. Seller notifications (if seller owner resolvable)
  if (sellerContact && sellerUserId) {
    // INV-S6-25: Seller dedup key is SEPARATE from buyer dedup key
    const dedupKeySeller = `notif:${sellerUserId}:OrderCreated:${orderId}`;
    const sellerAlreadyNotified = await ctx.deduplicationService.isDuplicate(dedupKeySeller);
    if (!sellerAlreadyNotified) {
      await ctx.notificationService.createAndEnqueue({
        userId: sellerUserId,
        contact: sellerContact,
        templateName: 'OrderCreated_SELLER',
        variables: vars,
        entityId: orderId,
        eventType: 'OrderCreated',
        channels: ['sms', 'email', 'inApp'],
      });
      // Set seller dedup AFTER successful enqueue
      await ctx.deduplicationService.setProcessed(dedupKeySeller, 300);
    }
  }

  // 6. Set buyer dedup key AFTER successful processing (INV-S6-6)
  await ctx.deduplicationService.setProcessed(dedupKeyBuyer, 300);
}
```

### §14.4 OrderStatusChanged Handler (Critical — Routing Logic)

```typescript
export async function handleOrderStatusChanged(
  payload: OrderStatusChangedPayload,
  ctx: HandlerContext,
): Promise<void> {
  const { orderId, buyerId, sellerId, statusTo, actorRole, trackingNumber, estimatedDelivery } = payload;

  // Routing table — statusTo → notification config
  const config = ORDER_STATUS_NOTIFICATION_CONFIG[statusTo];
  if (!config) {
    ctx.logger.debug({ statusTo }, 'ORDER_STATUS_NO_NOTIFICATION_CONFIG');
    return; // No notification for this status (e.g. DELIVERED, COMPLETED — Sprint 7)
  }

  const dedupKey = `notif:${buyerId}:OrderStatusChanged_${statusTo}:${orderId}`;
  if (await ctx.deduplicationService.isDuplicate(dedupKey)) return;

  const buyerContact = await ctx.userContactService.getContact(buyerId);
  const vars: Record<string, string> = {
    orderNumber: payload.orderNumber,
    ...(trackingNumber && { trackingNumber }),
    ...(estimatedDelivery && { estimatedDelivery }),
  };

  await ctx.notificationService.createAndEnqueue({
    userId: buyerId,
    contact: buyerContact,
    templateName: config.templateName,
    variables: vars,
    entityId: orderId,
    eventType: `OrderStatusChanged_${statusTo}`,
    channels: config.channels,
  });

  await ctx.deduplicationService.setProcessed(dedupKey, 300);
}

// Status → notification config map
const ORDER_STATUS_NOTIFICATION_CONFIG: Record<string, { templateName: string; channels: string[] }> = {
  CONFIRMED:   { templateName: 'OrderConfirmed_BUYER',    channels: ['sms', 'inApp'] },
  PROCESSING:  { templateName: 'OrderProcessing_BUYER',   channels: ['inApp'] },           // In-App only
  SHIPPED:     { templateName: 'OrderShipped_BUYER',      channels: ['sms', 'inApp'] },
  CANCELLED:   { templateName: 'OrderCancelled_BUYER',    channels: ['inApp'] },            // In-App only
  // DELIVERED: Sprint 7 Admin — no buyer notification here yet
  // COMPLETED: No notification — end state
};
```

### §14.5 SupplierScoreUpdated Handler (Score Threshold Filter)

```typescript
export async function handleSupplierScoreUpdated(
  payload: SupplierScoreUpdatedPayload,
  ctx: HandlerContext,
): Promise<void> {
  const { businessId, compositeScore, previousCompositeScore } = payload;

  // INV-S6-10: Only notify when score changes >= 5 points
  if (previousCompositeScore === null) return; // First score — no notification
  const scoreDelta = Math.abs(compositeScore - previousCompositeScore);
  if (scoreDelta < 5) {
    ctx.logger.debug({ businessId, scoreDelta }, 'SCORE_CHANGE_BELOW_THRESHOLD');
    return;
  }

  const sellerUserId = await ctx.userContactService.getBusinessOwnerUserId(businessId);
  if (!sellerUserId) return;

  const isImprovement = compositeScore > previousCompositeScore;
  const templateName = isImprovement ? 'ScoreImproved_SELLER' : 'ScoreDropped_SELLER';
  const channels = isImprovement ? ['inApp'] : ['sms', 'inApp'];  // Score drop: SMS

  const sellerContact = await ctx.userContactService.getContact(sellerUserId);

  const dedupKey = `notif:${sellerUserId}:SupplierScoreUpdated:${businessId}`;
  if (await ctx.deduplicationService.isDuplicate(dedupKey)) return;

  await ctx.notificationService.createAndEnqueue({
    userId: sellerUserId,
    contact: sellerContact,
    templateName,
    variables: {
      compositeScore: compositeScore.toString(),
      previousCompositeScore: previousCompositeScore.toString(),
      scoreDelta: scoreDelta.toString(),
    },
    entityId: businessId,
    eventType: 'SupplierScoreUpdated',
    channels,
  });

  await ctx.deduplicationService.setProcessed(dedupKey, 300);
}
```

### §14.6 Phase 3 Validation Gate

```
✅ OutboxConsumerWorker cron runs every 5 seconds (verify via logs)
✅ Cron overlap: if poll takes >5s, subsequent cron fires are skipped (OUTBOX_POLL_SKIPPED_OVERLAP in logs)
✅ OrderCreated event → buyer SMS + seller SMS + both In-App (verify)
✅ OrderCreated replay → buyer gets 1 notification, seller gets 1 notification (separate dedup keys — INV-S6-25)
✅ OrderStatusChanged CONFIRMED → buyer SMS + buyer In-App (verify)
✅ OrderStatusChanged PROCESSING → buyer In-App ONLY (no SMS)
✅ SupplierScoreUpdated score delta < 5 → no notification
✅ SupplierScoreUpdated score drops 7 pts → seller SMS + In-App
✅ Duplicate OrderCreated event within 5min → single buyer notification only (buyer dedup key)
✅ Duplicate OrderCreated event within 5min → single seller notification only (seller dedup key — INV-S6-25)
✅ Unknown eventType in EventOutbox → validatePayload returns failure → event COMPLETED with warn (INV-S6-27)
✅ Invalid EventOutbox payload → event marked FAILED, worker continues
✅ EventOutbox event marked COMPLETED only after BullMQ enqueue
```

**AI Footguns — Phase 3:**
```
FOOTGUN-3-A: Consuming both OrderConfirmed AND OrderStatusChanged CONFIRMED.
Fix: OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP must NOT contain 'OrderConfirmed'. Read INV-S6-13.

FOOTGUN-3-B: Calling handler.process(payload) with raw JSON — no Zod validation.
Fix: ALL payloads must go through validatePayload() using safeParse() before any handler is called.

FOOTGUN-3-C: Marking EventOutbox COMPLETED before BullMQ enqueue succeeds.
Fix: Read INV-S6-2 and the exact sequence in §14.2.

FOOTGUN-3-D: Handler throws on missing optional field (e.g., trackingNumber).
Fix: All optional fields use nullish coalescing: trackingNumber ?? null.

FOOTGUN-3-E: One handler error crashes entire batch.
Fix: Each event is processed in try/catch. One failure = markEventFailed() for that event, continue to next.

FOOTGUN-3-F: Using single dedup key for both buyer and seller in OrderCreated handler. (Hardening v1.1)
Fix: INV-S6-25 — buyer dedup key and seller dedup key are ALWAYS separate. Read §14.3.

FOOTGUN-3-G: Setting isPolling = false in catch block only (not in finally). (Hardening v1.1)
Fix: isPolling MUST be reset in finally block. An exception in processEvent leaves isPolling=true forever,
silently stopping all future outbox polling. This is a hidden total system failure.

FOOTGUN-3-H: validatePayload returning { success: true } for unknown event types. (Hardening v1.1)
Fix: INV-S6-27 — unknown event type has no schema. Return { success: false }. The no-handler branch
already handles unknown eventTypes before validatePayload is called (STEP 3 before STEP 4).
```

## §15 PHASE 4 — IN-APP NOTIFICATION SYSTEM

**Objective:** Synchronous In-App notification creation. DB-backed. No external dependency.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §15.1 In-App Creation (Synchronous — Not via BullMQ)

```typescript
// Inside NotificationService
async createInAppNotification(
  userId: string,
  templateName: string,
  language: 'hi' | 'en',
  variables: Record<string, string>,
  type: NotificationType,
): Promise<string> {
  // INV-S6-20: In-App is synchronous
  const template = await this.templateService.getTemplate(templateName, language);
  const title = this.templateService.render(template.title, variables);
  const body = this.templateService.render(template.body, variables);

  const { id } = await this.notificationRepository.create(userId, {
    type,
    title,
    body,
    channels: [NotificationChannel.IN_APP],
    metadata: { templateName, variables },
  });

  // Invalidate unread count cache
  await this.redis.del(`notif:unread-count:${userId}`).catch(() => {});

  return id; // Return notificationId for BullMQ job reference
}
```

### §15.2 Notification Center APIs

```typescript
@Controller('notifications')
@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard)
@Roles(UserRole.BUYER, UserRole.SELLER)
// NO SellerContextGuard — notifications are user-scoped (INV-S6-18)
export class NotificationController {

  @Get()
  async getNotifications(
    @Req() req: any,
    @Query(new ZodValidationPipe(NotificationListQuerySchema)) query: NotificationListQuery,
  ) {
    const userId = req.user.id; // JWT — never trust body
    return this.notificationService.getNotifications(userId, query);
  }

  @Get('unread-count')
  async getUnreadCount(@Req() req: any) {
    const userId = req.user.id;
    return { success: true, data: { count: await this.notificationService.getUnreadCount(userId) } };
  }

  @Patch('read-all')
  async markAllRead(@Req() req: any) {
    const userId = req.user.id;
    await this.notificationRepository.markAllRead(userId);
    await this.redis.del(`notif:unread-count:${userId}`).catch(() => {});
    return { success: true };
  }

  @Patch(':id/read')
  async markRead(@Req() req: any, @Param('id') notificationId: string) {
    const userId = req.user.id;
    // INV-S6-18: updateMany with userId filter prevents cross-user mark-read
    await this.notificationRepository.markRead(notificationId, userId);
    await this.redis.del(`notif:unread-count:${userId}`).catch(() => {});
    return { success: true };
  }
}
```

### §15.3 Phase 4 Validation Gate

```
✅ GET /notifications → returns only req.user's notifications (not others')
✅ PATCH /notifications/:id/read (other user's notification ID) → silently ignores (updateMany returns 0)
✅ PATCH /notifications/read-all → marks all user's unread as read
✅ GET /notifications/unread-count → correct count
✅ Notification stored in DB within 100ms of event processing
✅ notificationMonth field populated correctly (e.g., "2026-06")
```

**AI Footguns — Phase 4:**
```
FOOTGUN-4-A: Applying SellerContextGuard to notification routes.
Fix: NO SellerContextGuard on any notification route. Read INV-S6-18.

FOOTGUN-4-B: GET /notifications returns all notifications without userId filter.
Fix: EVERY NotificationRepository method must filter by userId.

FOOTGUN-4-C: Using OFFSET pagination instead of cursor.
Fix: Platform-wide rule: cursor pagination only. No skip/offset. See INV-S5-20 (inherited).
```

## §16 PHASE 5 — EMAIL DELIVERY SYSTEM

**Objective:** Transactional email via Resend. Independent from SMS. Retried via BullMQ.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §16.1 Email Channel Implementation

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/channels/email.channel.ts
export interface IEmailService {
  send(to: string, subject: string, htmlBody: string): Promise<EmailResult>;
}

export interface EmailResult {
  success: boolean;
  messageId?: string;
  error?: string;
}

export const EMAIL_SERVICE = Symbol('EMAIL_SERVICE');

@Injectable()
export class ResendEmailService implements IEmailService {
  private readonly resend: Resend;
  private readonly fromAddress: string;

  constructor(private readonly config: ConfigService) {
    this.resend = new Resend(config.get('RESEND_API_KEY'));
    this.fromAddress = config.get('EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS');
  }

  async send(to: string, subject: string, htmlBody: string): Promise<EmailResult> {
    try {
      const { data, error } = await this.resend.emails.send({
        from: this.fromAddress,
        to: [to],
        subject,
        html: htmlBody,
      });
      if (error) return { success: false, error: error.message };
      return { success: true, messageId: data?.id };
    } catch (err) {
      return { success: false, error: (err as Error).message };
    }
  }
}
```

### §16.2 Email HTML Template

```typescript
// INV-S6-23: HTML-entity-escape all user-controlled variables before HTML injection
// TemplateService.sanitize() strips dangerous chars for SMS/plain-text context.
// htmlEscape() is a SEPARATE function for HTML context — applied to title, body, CTA text.
function htmlEscape(str: string): string {
  return str
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;')
    .replace(/"/g, '&quot;')
    .replace(/'/g, '&#x27;');
}

// Template renders to HTML with VyaparNet branding
// Mobile-first, Hinglish subject, plain text fallback
function buildEmailHtml(title: string, body: string, ctaUrl?: string, ctaText?: string): string {
  // INV-S6-23: Escape ALL user-controlled values before injection into HTML
  const safeTitle = htmlEscape(title);
  const safeBody = htmlEscape(body);
  // ctaUrl: validate against allowlist of internal paths (not injected from user input directly)
  // ctaText: escape if user-provided
  const safeCtaText = ctaText ? htmlEscape(ctaText) : 'View Details';

  return `<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>${safeTitle}</title>
</head>
<body style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background: #f5f5f5; margin: 0; padding: 20px;">
  <div style="max-width: 600px; margin: 0 auto; background: white; border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden;">
    <div style="background: #6C3CF7; padding: 20px; text-align: center;">
      <h1 style="color: white; margin: 0; font-size: 24px;">VyaparNet</h1>
    </div>
    <div style="padding: 24px;">
      <h2 style="color: #1a1a1a; margin-bottom: 12px;">${safeTitle}</h2>
      <p style="color: #555; line-height: 1.6;">${safeBody}</p>
      ${ctaUrl ? `<a href="${ctaUrl}" style="display:inline-block;background:#6C3CF7;color:white;padding:12px 24px;border-radius:6px;text-decoration:none;margin-top:16px;">${safeCtaText}</a>` : ''}
    </div>
    <div style="padding: 16px 24px; border-top: 1px solid #eee; font-size: 12px; color: #999;">
      <p>VyaparNet &mdash; Aapka B2B Marketplace</p>
      <p><!-- Unsubscribe: use notification preferences at /notifications/preferences --></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</body>
</html>`;
}
```

> **INV-S6-23 Note:** The `{{unsubscribeUrl}}` literal from the original template has been removed. Sprint 6 uses the `/notifications/preferences` API for opt-out (INV-S6-5 preference-gating). A one-click email unsubscribe link (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe) is a Sprint 8 email platform concern when email volumes justify it.

## §17 PHASE 6 — SMS DELIVERY SYSTEM

**Objective:** Reuse Sprint 1 SmsService. Wrap for notification context. Independent BullMQ job.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §17.1 SMS Channel Implementation

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/channels/sms.channel.ts
@Injectable()
export class SmsChannel implements INotificationChannel {
  name = 'sms' as const;
  private readonly logger = new Logger(SmsChannel.name);

  constructor(
    @Inject(SMS_SERVICE) private readonly smsService: SmsService, // Sprint 1 interface
  ) {}

  async send(job: NotificationJob): Promise<void> {
    if (!job.phone) {
      // INV-S6-16: null phone = skip + warn, never throw
      this.logger.warn({ userId: job.userId }, 'SMS_SKIPPED_NO_PHONE');
      return;
    }

    const result = await this.smsService.sendTransactional(job.phone, job.body);
    // Note: Sprint 1 SmsService.sendOtp() signature is for OTP only.
    // Sprint 6 needs sendTransactional() — extends the interface.
    if (!result.success) {
      throw new Error(`SMS delivery failed: ${result.error}`);
      // BullMQ catches this → retry 3x → DLQ
    }
  }
}
```

### §17.2 Extending SmsService Interface

The Sprint 1 `SmsService` interface has only `sendOtp()`. Sprint 6 requires `sendTransactional()`.

```typescript
// EXTEND (not replace) apps/api/src/modules/identity/auth/sms.service.interface.ts
export interface SmsService {
  sendOtp(phoneNumber: string, otp: string): Promise<SmsResult>;
  sendTransactional(phoneNumber: string, message: string): Promise<SmsResult>; // Sprint 6 addition
}
```

`Msg91SmsService` must implement `sendTransactional()` using the same `SmsProviderStrategy` pattern.

## §18 PHASE 7 — PUSH NOTIFICATION SYSTEM

**Objective:** Web Push via VAPID. Multi-device. Best-effort (no DLQ).

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §18.1 WebPushService Implementation

```typescript
@Injectable()
export class WebPushService {
  constructor(
    private readonly config: ConfigService,
    private readonly pushSubscriptionRepository: PushSubscriptionRepository,
  ) {
    webpush.setVapidDetails(
      `mailto:${config.get('VAPID_EMAIL')}`,
      config.get('VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY'),
      config.get('VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY'),
    );
  }

  async sendToUser(userId: string, title: string, body: string, url?: string): Promise<void> {
    const subscriptions = await this.pushSubscriptionRepository.getActiveForUser(userId);
    if (subscriptions.length === 0) return;

    const payload = JSON.stringify({ title, body, url, icon: '/icons/icon-192.png' });

    // Send to all devices (multi-device support)
    await Promise.allSettled(
      subscriptions.map(sub => this.sendToSubscription(sub, payload))
    );
  }

  private async sendToSubscription(
    sub: PushSubscriptionRow,
    payload: string,
  ): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await webpush.sendNotification(
        { endpoint: sub.endpoint, keys: { p256dh: sub.p256dh, auth: sub.auth } },
        payload,
        { TTL: 3600 },
      );
    } catch (err: any) {
      if (err.statusCode === 410) {
        // INV-S6-9: 410 Gone = stale subscription, delete immediately
        await this.pushSubscriptionRepository.deleteByEndpoint(sub.endpoint, sub.userId);
        this.logger.warn({ userId: sub.userId, endpoint: sub.endpoint.slice(-20) }, 'PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION_DELETED_STALE');
      }
      // Other errors: log and swallow (push is best-effort)
      this.logger.warn({ error: (err as Error).message }, 'PUSH_DELIVERY_FAILED');
    }
  }
}
```

### §18.2 Push Subscription Controller

```typescript
@Post('push/subscribe')
async subscribe(
  @Req() req: any,
  @Body(new ZodValidationPipe(PushSubscribeSchema)) dto: PushSubscribeDto,
) {
  const userId = req.user.id;
  // INV-S6-22: Cap enforcement is inside repository.upsert()
  await this.pushSubscriptionRepository.upsert(userId, dto);
  return { success: true };
}

  @Req() req: any,
  // INV-S6-29: Zod validation REQUIRED on unsubscribe body
  @Body(new ZodValidationPipe(PushUnsubscribeSchema)) body: PushUnsubscribeDto,
) {

  await this.pushSubscriptionRepository.deleteByEndpoint(body.endpoint, userId);
  return { success: true };
}

@Get('push/vapid-public-key')

async getVapidPublicKey() {

}
```

### §18.2a PushSubscriptionRepository — Cap Enforcement Contract (INV-S6-22)

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/notification/repositories/push-subscription.repository.ts
async upsert(userId: string, dto: PushSubscribeDto): Promise<void> {
  // INV-S6-22: Max 10 active push subscriptions per user
  // Prevents amplification attack: malicious user subscribing 1000 endpoints
  const PUSH_SUB_CAP = 10;

  await this.prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    // Count active subscriptions for this user
    const activeCount = await tx.pushSubscription.count({
      where: { userId, isActive: true },
    });

    if (activeCount >= PUSH_SUB_CAP) {
      // Delete oldest subscription to make room for new one
      const oldest = await tx.pushSubscription.findFirst({
        where: { userId, isActive: true },
        orderBy: { createdAt: 'asc' },
        select: { id: true },
      });
      if (oldest) {
        await tx.pushSubscription.delete({ where: { id: oldest.id } });
        this.logger.warn({ userId, deletedId: oldest.id }, 'PUSH_SUB_CAP_EVICTION');
      }
    }

    // Upsert the subscription (update keys if endpoint already registered)
    await tx.pushSubscription.upsert({
      where: { uq_push_sub_user_endpoint: { userId, endpoint: dto.endpoint } },
      create: {
        userId,
        endpoint: dto.endpoint,
        p256dh: dto.keys.p256dh,
        auth: dto.keys.auth,
        userAgent: dto.userAgent ?? null,
        isActive: true,
      },
      update: {
        p256dh: dto.keys.p256dh,
        auth: dto.keys.auth,
        userAgent: dto.userAgent ?? null,
        isActive: true,
        updatedAt: new Date(),
      },
    });
  });
}
```

### §18.3 Environment Variables Required

```
VAPID_EMAIL=support@vyaparnet.com
VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=<generated with web-push generate-vapid-keys>
VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=<generated with web-push generate-vapid-keys>
```

### §18.4 Phase 7 Validation Gate

```
✅ GET /notifications/push/vapid-public-key → public key returned
✅ POST /notifications/push/subscribe → subscription stored in PushSubscription table
✅ POST /notifications/push/subscribe (invalid endpoint) → 400 validation error (INV-S6-29)
✅ POST /notifications/push/subscribe (11th subscription for same user) → oldest subscription evicted (INV-S6-22)
✅ DELETE /notifications/push/unsubscribe (invalid body: no endpoint) → 400 (INV-S6-29)
✅ DELETE /notifications/push/unsubscribe (valid) → subscription removed (INV-S6-29)
✅ Push notification sent to subscribed buyer when order shipped
✅ 410 Gone response → subscription deleted immediately
✅ No VAPID private key in logs
✅ Multiple device subscriptions: push sent to all devices
✅ Push failure → logged as warn, not error (best-effort channel)
✅ PUSH_SUB_CAP_EVICTION log appears when cap exceeded
```

## §19 PHASE 8 — NOTIFICATION PREFERENCES

**Objective:** User-controlled per-channel-per-type preferences. JSONB storage. Redis cached.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §19.1 NotificationPreferenceService

```typescript
@Injectable()
export class NotificationPreferenceService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(NotificationPreferenceService.name);

  constructor(
    private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
    private readonly redis: RedisService,
  ) {}

  async getPreferences(userId: string): Promise<NotificationPreference> {
    // Redis cache first (INV-S6 — Redis is optimization, not authority)
    try {
      const cached = await this.redis.get(`notif:pref:${userId}`);
      if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached) as NotificationPreference;
    } catch {
      this.logger.warn({ userId }, 'PREF_REDIS_CACHE_MISS');
    }

    // DB fallback
    const user = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
      where: { id: userId },
      select: { notificationPreferences: true }, // JSONB field
    });

    const prefs = (user?.notificationPreferences as NotificationPreference | null)
      ?? DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCES;

    // Validate against schema (JSONB may have old/partial shape)
    const parsed = NotificationPreferenceSchema.safeParse(prefs);
    const validated = parsed.success ? parsed.data : DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCES;

    // Cache
    await this.redis.set(`notif:pref:${userId}`, JSON.stringify(validated), 'EX', 300).catch(() => {});

    return validated;
  }

  async updatePreferences(userId: string, dto: UpdatePreferencesDto): Promise<NotificationPreference> {
    await this.prisma.user.update({
      where: { id: userId },
      data: { notificationPreferences: dto as any },
    });
    // Invalidate cache
    await this.redis.del(`notif:pref:${userId}`).catch(() => {});
    return dto;
  }

  // Used by NotificationWorker — channel delivery gating (INV-S6-5)
  isChannelEnabled(
    prefs: NotificationPreference,
    channel: 'sms' | 'email' | 'push' | 'inApp',
    eventCategory: 'orderUpdates' | 'paymentUpdates' | 'scorecard' | 'lowStock',
  ): boolean {
    return prefs[channel]?.[eventCategory] ?? false;
  }
}
```

### §19.3 Preference Check in NotificationService.createAndEnqueue()

```typescript
async createAndEnqueue(params: CreateAndEnqueueParams): Promise<void> {
  const { userId, contact, templateName, variables, entityId, eventType, channels } = params;

  // INV-S6-5: Preference check is FIRST operation
  const prefs = await this.preferenceService.getPreferences(userId);

  // Determine event category from templateName
  const category = this.getEventCategory(eventType);

  // Always create In-App (ground truth — INV-S6-20)
  const notificationId = await this.createInAppNotification(userId, templateName, contact.preferredLanguage, variables, this.getNotificationType(eventType));

  // Channel delivery — each independent (INV-S6-8)
  const jobs: NotificationJob[] = [];

  if (channels.includes('sms') && this.preferenceService.isChannelEnabled(prefs, 'sms', category)) {
    // INV-S6-16: verify phone non-null
    if (contact.phone) {
      jobs.push({ channel: 'sms', userId, notificationId, templateName, variables, phone: contact.phone });
    }
  }

  if (channels.includes('email') && this.preferenceService.isChannelEnabled(prefs, 'email', category)) {
    if (contact.email) {
      jobs.push({ channel: 'email', userId, notificationId, templateName, variables, email: contact.email });
    }
  }

  if (channels.includes('push') && this.preferenceService.isChannelEnabled(prefs, 'push', category)) {
    jobs.push({ channel: 'push', userId, notificationId, templateName, variables });
  }

  // Enqueue independently (INV-S6-8)
  await Promise.allSettled(
    jobs.map(job => this.notificationsQueue.add(`deliver-${job.channel}`, job))
  );
}
```

### §19.4 Phase 8 Validation Gate

```
✅ GET /notifications/preferences → returns current preferences (or defaults)
✅ PUT /notifications/preferences → updates and invalidates Redis cache
✅ Preference SMS=false → no SMS job enqueued for order events
✅ Preference email=false → no email sent
✅ In-App always created regardless of SMS/email preference
✅ Default preferences match DL-20 values (scorecard SMS=false, lowStock email=false)
✅ Redis cache miss → falls back to DB (no 500)
✅ Invalid JSONB in DB → falls back to DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCES (no crash)
```

## §20 PHASE 9 — TEMPLATE MANAGEMENT

**Objective:** Pre-compiled template service. Safe rendering. DB-backed. No dynamic code.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §20.1 TemplateService

```typescript
@Injectable()
export class TemplateService implements OnModuleInit {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(TemplateService.name);
  // In-memory compiled template cache — loaded once at startup (INV-S6-14-note: SC.5)
  private readonly templateCache = new Map<string, CompiledTemplate>();

  constructor(
    private readonly notificationTemplateRepository: NotificationTemplateRepository,
  ) {}

  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.compileAllTemplates();
    this.logger.log(`TemplateService: ${this.templateCache.size} templates compiled`);
  }

  private async compileAllTemplates(): Promise<void> {
    const templates = await this.notificationTemplateRepository.findAllActive();
    for (const template of templates) {
      this.templateCache.set(`${template.name}_hi`, {
        title: template.titleHi,
        body: template.bodyHi,
        type: template.type,
      });
      this.templateCache.set(`${template.name}_en`, {
        title: template.titleEn,
        body: template.bodyEn,
        type: template.type,
      });
    }
  }

  getTemplate(name: string, language: 'hi' | 'en'): CompiledTemplate {
    const key = `${name}_${language}`;
    const template = this.templateCache.get(key)
      ?? this.templateCache.get(`${name}_hi`); // Fallback to Hindi

    if (!template) {
      this.logger.error({ templateName: name, language }, 'TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND');
      // Fallback: generic message (never crash worker)
      return {
        title: language === 'hi' ? 'VyaparNet se update' : 'Update from VyaparNet',
        body: language === 'hi' ? 'Aapke account mein kuch hua hai.' : 'Something happened in your account.',
        type: NotificationType.SYSTEM,
      };
    }
    return template;
  }

  // INV-S6-14: Safe substitution ONLY. No eval. No template literals.
  render(template: string, variables: Record<string, string>): string {
    let result = template;
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(variables)) {
      const sanitized = this.sanitize(value);
      result = result.replaceAll(`{{${key}}}`, sanitized);
    }
    // Catch any unreplaced variables — replace with empty string
    result = result.replace(/\{\{[a-zA-Z0-9_]+\}\}/g, '');
    return result.trim();
  }

  private sanitize(value: string): string {
    return String(value)
      .replace(/[<>'"&]/g, '')          // Strip HTML-dangerous chars
      .replace(/[~^{}|\\]/g, '')        // Strip SMS-dangerous chars
      .slice(0, 200);                    // Max 200 chars per variable
  }
}
```

### §20.2 Phase 9 Validation Gate

```
✅ All 11+ templates loaded at startup (verify log: "X templates compiled")
✅ Template render replaces {{orderNumber}} correctly
✅ Template render strips HTML tags from variable values
✅ Unknown template name → fallback message (no crash)
✅ Unreplaced {{variable}} → replaced with empty string (not left in message)
✅ Template body <= 160 chars for SMS templates (verify each SMS template)
```
