## §21 PHASE 10 — RETRY & DLQ ARCHITECTURE

**Objective:** Resilient delivery with 3 retries, DLQ for undeliverable jobs.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Flash

### §21.1 NotificationWorker (BullMQ Processor)

```typescript
@Processor('notifications')
@Injectable()
export class NotificationWorker {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(NotificationWorker.name);

  constructor(
    private readonly smsChannel: SmsChannel,
    private readonly emailChannel: EmailChannel,
    private readonly webPushService: WebPushService,
    private readonly metrics: NotificationMetricsService,
  ) {}

  @Process({ name: 'deliver-sms', concurrency: 5 })
  async deliverSms(job: Job<NotificationJob>): Promise<void> {
    await this.deliverWithMetrics('sms', job.data, () =>
      this.smsChannel.send(job.data)
    );
  }

  @Process({ name: 'deliver-email', concurrency: 3 })
  async deliverEmail(job: Job<NotificationJob>): Promise<void> {
    await this.deliverWithMetrics('email', job.data, () =>
      this.emailChannel.send(job.data)
    );
  }

  @Process({ name: 'deliver-push', concurrency: 5 })
  async deliverPush(job: Job<NotificationJob>): Promise<void> {
    // Push: best-effort, no throw (INV-S6: push is best-effort)
    try {
      await this.webPushService.sendToUser(
        job.data.userId,
        job.data.title,
        job.data.body,
      );
      this.metrics.notificationSentTotal.inc({ channel: 'push', eventType: job.data.eventType });
    } catch (err) {
      // Push: log warn, do NOT rethrow (no retry, no DLQ for push)
      this.logger.warn({ error: (err as Error).message }, 'PUSH_DELIVERY_FAILED_SILENCED');
    }
  }

  @OnQueueFailed()
  onJobFailed(job: Job<NotificationJob>, err: Error): void {
    this.logger.error({
      jobId: job.id, channel: job.data?.channel, userId: job.data?.userId,
      attempt: job.attemptsMade, error: err.message,
    }, 'NOTIFICATION_JOB_FAILED');

    if (job.attemptsMade >= 3) {
      // Job will move to DLQ (notifications-failed queue)
      this.metrics.notificationDlqSize.inc();
      this.logger.error({ jobId: job.id }, 'NOTIFICATION_DLQ');
    }
  }

  private async deliverWithMetrics(
    channel: string,
    data: NotificationJob,
    deliverFn: () => Promise<void>,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const start = Date.now();
    try {
      await deliverFn();
      this.metrics.notificationSentTotal.inc({ channel, eventType: data.eventType ?? 'unknown' });
    } catch (err) {
      this.metrics.notificationFailedTotal.inc({ channel, reason: 'provider_error', eventType: data.eventType ?? 'unknown' });
      throw err; // Re-throw for BullMQ retry
    } finally {
      this.metrics.notificationOutboxToDeliveryMs.observe(Date.now() - start);
    }
  }
}
```

### §21.2 DLQ Strategy

**DLQ Queue Name:** `notifications-failed` — LOCKED. This is the authoritative name.

> **AF-3 Audit Fix:** "decision for implementer" is NEVER acceptable in an execution lock document. The DLQ queue name is hereby locked. Implementer MUST NOT use `dead-letter`, `notification-dlq`, or any other name.

```typescript
// 'notifications-failed' queue — LOCKED queue name
// Register in BullMQModule alongside 'notifications' queue:
// BullModule.registerQueue({ name: 'notifications' }, { name: 'notifications-failed' })
//
// BullMQ job configuration defaultJobOptions.failedJobSettings:
// After 3 failed attempts → job automatically moves to 'notifications-failed'
// (BullMQ handles this automatically with removeOnFail: false + defaultJobOptions.attempts: 3)

// Manual DLQ replay (Sprint 7 Admin tool):
// GET /admin/notifications/dlq → list failed jobs from 'notifications-failed'
// POST /admin/notifications/dlq/:jobId/replay → move back to 'notifications' queue
```

**Environment variable required:**
```
# No extra env var needed — queue name is hardcoded: 'notifications-failed'
```

### §21.3 Phase 10 Validation Gate

```
✅ SMS failure → BullMQ logs retry attempt
✅ SMS fails 3 times → job moves to DLQ
✅ notification_dlq_size gauge increments
✅ Email failure retried independently (not blocked by SMS DLQ)
✅ Push failure → silenced, not retried, not DLQ'd
```

## §22 PHASE 11 — NOTIFICATION CENTER (USER-FACING)

**Objective:** Complete notification bell UI + preference management. Frontend integration spec.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Pro (complex UX patterns)

### §22.1 Frontend Integration Spec (OpenAPI contract)

Notification bell polling strategy (implemented in frontend, not backend):
```
Interval: 30 seconds
Endpoint: GET /notifications/unread-count
On success: update badge count
On error: silent fail (no banner)
On badge > 0: show notification panel on next user interaction
```

Notification panel:
```
On panel open: fetch GET /notifications (limit=20)
On scroll to bottom: fetch with cursor
On tap notification: PATCH /notifications/:id/read → navigate to deep link
On "mark all read": PATCH /notifications/read-all
```

### §22.2 Notification Deep Links

Each notification metadata MUST include a deep link URL:
```typescript
// In metadata field:
metadata: {
  templateName,
  entityId,     // orderId, productId, etc.
  deepLink: '/buyer/orders/{orderId}',   // Frontend route
}
```

Deep link mapping:
```
OrderCreated_BUYER → /buyer/orders/{orderId}
OrderShipped_BUYER → /buyer/orders/{orderId}
PaymentFailed_BUYER → /buyer/orders/{orderId}/payment-retry
OrderCreated_SELLER → /seller/orders/{orderId}
ScoreDropped_SELLER → /seller/scorecard
StockLow_SELLER → /seller/inventory
```

### §22.3 Phase 11 Validation Gate

```
✅ GET /notifications returns notifications with correct deepLink in metadata
✅ Notifications are ordered by id DESC (CUID — equivalent to newest-first due to monotonic sort) (INV-S6-24)
✅ hasMore: true when >20 notifications
✅ nextCursor (CUID id) allows fetching next page correctly (no duplicates, no skips)
✅ PATCH /notifications/read-all marks all as read and returns 200
✅ Unread count correctly reflects reads
✅ NotificationJob.body and NotificationJob.title pre-rendered at enqueue time — worker uses job.data.body directly
```

> **AF-8 Audit Fix:** "ordered by createdAt DESC" corrected to "ordered by id DESC (CUID)" — consistent with INV-S6-24 and repository implementation in §13.2. CUIDs are monotonically sortable so ordering by id DESC produces the same visual result (newest first) without the non-uniqueness risk of createdAt.

### §23.2 Operational Runbooks

**Runbook: OutboxConsumerWorker Stopped**
```
Alert: notification_outbox_consumed_total rate == 0 for 10min
Check: Worker process alive? BullMQ connection? Redis connection?
Fix: Restart apps/api container. Worker restarts with EVERY_5_SECONDS cron.
Risk: PENDING EventOutbox events pile up. On restart, processed in FIFO order. Dedup prevents doubles.
```

**Runbook: SMS Failure Rate > 10%**
```
Alert: notification_failed_total{channel="sms"} rate > 10%
Check: MSG91 status page. Rate limits? Account balance? Template approval?
Fix: Check SmsProviderStrategy. Switch to Twilio backup if needed.
```

**Runbook: DLQ Size > 100**
```
Alert: notification_dlq_size > 100
Check: What eventType/channel is failing? Provider outage?
Fix: Resolve provider issue. Manual DLQ replay in Sprint 7 Admin.
```

## §24 PHASE 13 — SECURITY HARDENING

**Objective:** PII protection, ownership enforcement, template injection prevention, push security.

**Best Model:** Gemini 2.5 Pro (security-critical)

### §24.1 Security Invariant Checklist

For EVERY NotificationController route:
```
✅ JwtAuthGuard is global (inherited from AppModule)
✅ @Roles(UserRole.BUYER, UserRole.SELLER) present
✅ NO SellerContextGuard (notifications are user-scoped)
✅ userId extracted from req.user.id (JWT) — NEVER from request body or params
✅ All DB queries filter by userId (INV-S6-18)
```

### §24.2 PII Protection Implementation

```typescript
// In all logger calls:
// FORBIDDEN:
this.logger.info({ phone: user.phone, email: user.email }, 'SMS_SENT'); // PII LEAK

// CORRECT:
this.logger.info({
  phoneLastFour: user.phone?.slice(-4),
  emailDomain: user.email?.split('@')[1],
  userId: user.id,
}, 'SMS_SENT');
```

### §24.3 Template Injection Test Cases

Required unit tests in `template.service.spec.ts`:
```typescript
it('sanitizes HTML in variables', () => {
  const result = service.render('Hello {{name}}', { name: '<script>alert(1)</script>' });
  expect(result).toBe('Hello scriptalert(1)/script'); // HTML stripped
});

it('sanitizes SMS dangerous chars', () => {
  const result = service.render('Order {{orderNumber}}', { orderNumber: 'VN~123^456' });
  expect(result).toBe('Order VN123456'); // ~ and ^ stripped
});

it('handles missing variables gracefully', () => {
  const result = service.render('Hello {{name}}, order {{orderNumber}}', { name: 'Akash' });
  expect(result).toBe('Hello Akash, order '); // {{orderNumber}} replaced with empty
});
```

### §24.4 Seller Privacy (INV-S6-7)

Seller notifications MUST NOT contain buyer PII:
- `OrderCreated_SELLER` body: "Naya order aaya! ₹{grandTotal}" — NO buyer name, NO buyer phone
- Seller sees: `buyerCode` (masked) in their dashboard (Sprint 5 contract), NOT in notifications

### §24.5 Phase 13 Validation Gate

```
✅ GET /notifications with another user's JWT → returns only own notifications
✅ PATCH /notifications/:othersId/read → silently ignores (no error, no cross-user mutation)
✅ Template rendered with <script> input → HTML stripped from SMS output (TemplateService.sanitize)
✅ buildEmailHtml('<script>evil</script>') → rendered as '&lt;script&gt;evil&lt;/script&gt;' in email HTML (INV-S6-23)
✅ No phone number in logs (grep "phone" in notification module → 0 plaintext hits)
✅ No email address in logs (grep "email" in notification module → 0 plaintext hits)
✅ Seller notification body has no buyer name/phone (INV-S6-7)
✅ VAPID private key not in logs (grep VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY → 0 hits)
✅ POST /notifications/push/subscribe with wrong userId → owns only own subscriptions
✅ DELETE /notifications/push/unsubscribe with no endpoint body → 400 (INV-S6-29)
✅ POST /notifications/push/subscribe (11th device) → oldest subscription evicted, not 400 (INV-S6-22)
```

```
✅ Subscribe → PushSubscription row created
```

```
✅ GET /notifications (no JWT) → 401
✅ GET /notifications (ADMIN role) → 403 (not allowed — ADMIN is Sprint 7)
✅ PATCH /notifications/:othersId/read → 200 with no effect (ownership enforced at DB layer)
✅ POST /notifications/push/subscribe (no JWT) → 401
✅ Template with {{unreplaced}} in rendered output → FAIL (unreplaced vars must be empty)
✅ Notification list cursor: passing previous nextCursor → correct next page (no duplicates, no skips) (INV-S6-24)
✅ Notification list: 2 notifications created in same millisecond → both appear on correct pages (INV-S6-24)
```

### §25.8 Functional Gate — Observability

```
✅ notification_sent_total{channel="sms"} increments on SMS send
✅ notification_failed_total increments on SMS failure
✅ notification_dedup_skipped_total increments on dedup
✅ notification_outbox_consumed_total increments per event processed
✅ DLQ alert fires when notification_dlq_size > 100 (verify in Grafana)
✅ /metrics endpoint includes all Sprint 6 metrics
✅ cb_state{channel="sms"} == 1 after 5 consecutive SMS failures (INV-S6-21)
```

### §25.9 Functional Gate — Operational

```
✅ OutboxConsumerWorker stops → EventOutbox events remain PENDING (no data loss)
✅ OutboxConsumerWorker restarts → PENDING events re-processed within 10s
✅ Duplicate event processed after restart → single notification (idempotency key)
✅ SMS provider mock returns error → job retried 3x → DLQ
✅ Email provider mock returns error → job retried 3x → DLQ (independent of SMS)
✅ Push returns 410 → subscription deleted, no DLQ
✅ Long batch poll (>5s) → next cron cycle skipped (OUTBOX_POLL_SKIPPED_OVERLAP log) (INV-S6-26)
✅ 5 consecutive SMS failures → circuit opens → 6th SMS silently skipped, not enqueued for retry (INV-S6-21)
✅ 120s after circuit opens → circuit auto-closes → SMS delivery resumes (INV-S6-21)
✅ Template seed on 2nd startup → template bodyHi/titleHi unchanged in DB (INV-S6-28)
✅ 10 push subscriptions active, 11th subscribe → oldest evicted, new one stored (INV-S6-22)
```

## §26 SPRINT 6 ENTERPRISE SELF-AUDIT

### §26.1 Ownership Leaks — VERIFIED CLEAN

| Concern | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| NotificationModule imports OrderService | ❌ FORBIDDEN — BLOCKED | Module boundary: no domain service imports |
| NotificationModule writes to EventOutbox | ❌ FORBIDDEN — BLOCKED | INV-S6-1 + zero write paths in architecture |
| NotificationModule reads Order table directly | ❌ FORBIDDEN — BLOCKED | All data from EventOutbox payload |
| SellerContextGuard on notification routes | ❌ FORBIDDEN — BLOCKED | INV-S6-18 documented |
| Seller sees buyer phone in notification | ❌ FORBIDDEN — BLOCKED | INV-S6-7 + template audit |

### §26.2 EventOutbox Violations — VERIFIED CLEAN

| Concern | Status |
|---|---|
| Sprint 6 writes EventOutbox events | ❌ ZERO WRITES — pure consumer |
| Event marked COMPLETED before BullMQ enqueue | ❌ BLOCKED by INV-S6-2 + sequence documented |
| Duplicate EventOutbox event causes double notification | ❌ BLOCKED by INV-S6-17 (Redis idempotency) + INV-S6-6 (dedup) |
| OrderConfirmed consumed alongside OrderStatusChanged | ❌ BLOCKED by INV-S6-13 |

### §26.3 Redis Governance — VERIFIED CLEAN

| Concern | Status |
|---|---|
| Redis used as source of truth for preferences | ❌ BLOCKED — always DB fallback |
| Redis failure blocks notification delivery | ❌ BLOCKED — all Redis ops in try/catch |
| Dedup key uses Date.now() | ❌ BLOCKED by INV-S6-6 |
| Circuit breaker assumes OPEN on Redis failure | ❌ BLOCKED by INV-S6-21 — CLOSED assumed on Redis failure |
| Circuit breaker Redis keys missing TTL | ❌ BLOCKED — cb:open TTL=120s, cb:failures TTL=60s |

### §26.4 Scaling Bottlenecks — VERIFIED CLEAN

| Concern | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| OutboxConsumerWorker processes all events sequentially | 50-event batches, Redis lock per event, concurrent multi-instance safe |
| Cron fires overlap if batch takes >5s | INV-S6-26: isPolling guard — overlapping cycles are skipped |
| Template cache invalidation on update | Restart required (acceptable for MVP — infrequent) |
| Notification table unbounded growth | notificationMonth partition + 90-day archive policy |
| PushSubscription table stale entries | 410 Gone → immediate delete (INV-S6-9) |
| PushSubscription amplification attack (1000 endpoints) | INV-S6-22: hard cap at 10 per user, oldest evicted on exceed |
| In-App notification count query is full scan | Capped at 100 (§13.2), indexed by userId+isRead+createdAt |
| Cursor pagination fails under concurrent inserts | INV-S6-24: CUID cursor (not createdAt), monotonically sortable |

### §26.5 No Sprint 7/8/9 Blockers — VERIFIED

| Concern | Status |
|---|---|
| Sprint 7 AdminNotificationService needs access | ✅ NotificationService.sendDirect() is exported |
| Sprint 7 KYC approval notification | ✅ OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP extensible — add KycApproved handler |
| Sprint 8 ReturnInitiated notification | ✅ Add ReturnInitiatedPayloadSchema to types + handler to map |
| Sprint 9 analytics indexing | ✅ notificationMonth partition field ready (UTC-computed — INV-S6-30) |
| WhatsApp Phase 2 | ✅ INotificationChannel interface: add 'whatsapp' to union |
| CircuitBreakerService adds new Redis keys | ✅ Fully namespaced under cb: prefix — zero collision with Sprint 1-5 keys |

### §26.6 AI-Agent Ambiguity — ZERO AMBIGUOUS POINTS

All 30 invariants (INV-S6-1 through INV-S6-30) are explicit with enforcement layer documented. All AI footguns (FOOTGUN-0-A through FOOTGUN-3-H + Phase 4-14 footguns) are documented with exact fixes. No handwavy guidance.

### §26.7 Hardening v1.1 Additions — VERIFIED CLOSED

| Attack Vector | Hardening Applied | Invariant |
|---|---|---|
| SMS/Email retry storm on provider outage | Channel Circuit Breaker (CLOSED→OPEN at 5 failures/60s, auto-reset 120s) | INV-S6-21 |
| Push subscription amplification attack | Max 10 subscriptions per user, oldest evicted | INV-S6-22 |
| Email HTML injection via template variables | `htmlEscape()` applied to all template vars before HTML injection | INV-S6-23 |
| Cursor pagination breaks at millisecond-precision duplicates | Cursor uses CUID `id`, not `createdAt` | INV-S6-24 |
| Seller receives duplicate notifications on event replay | Separate seller dedup key in every handler | INV-S6-25 |
| Cron overlap — concurrent batch processing | `isPolling` flag guards cron entry, released in finally | INV-S6-26 |
| Unknown event type passes through as valid payload | `validatePayload()` returns `{ success: false }` for unknown schemas | INV-S6-27 |
| Template body silently overwritten on startup | Seed upsert uses empty `update: { isActive }` — body never overwritten | INV-S6-28 |
| Unsubscribe endpoint accepts unvalidated null endpoint | `PushUnsubscribeSchema` Zod validation via `ZodValidationPipe` | INV-S6-29 |
| `notificationMonth` timezone drift (IST vs UTC) | `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7)` — always UTC | INV-S6-30 |
| `{{unsubscribeUrl}}` literal rendered in emails | Removed. Preferences API used for opt-out. RFC 8058 deferred to Sprint 8 | INV-S6-23 Note |
| `PaymentReceived` missing `sellerId` in payload | Documented: seller lookup not required for payment events (buyer-only) | Architecture |

## §27 UNIVERSAL AGENT IMPLEMENTATION PROMPT

```
You are implementing SPRINT 6 — NOTIFICATION PLATFORM for VyaparNet.

MANDATORY READING BEFORE ANY CODE:
1. SPRINT_6_EXECUTION_LOCK_FINAL.md §0 — All invariants. Read ALL 30. Non-negotiable.
2. SPRINT_6_SCOPE_DECISIONS.md — What is IN and OUT.
3. packages/types/src/events/outbox-payloads.schemas.ts — Payload schemas.
4. packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma — Notification, NotificationTemplate, User models.
5. apps/api/src/modules/identity/auth/sms.service.interface.ts — SmsService interface.

ABSOLUTE RULES:
- NotificationModule is a PURE CONSUMER. NEVER writes EventOutbox. NEVER imports domain services.
- ALL payload reads use safeParse(). NEVER parse(). Invalid payload: log + mark FAILED + continue.
- Preference check is FIRST in every delivery path.
- In-App notification is SYNCHRONOUS. SMS/Email/Push are BullMQ jobs.
- Each channel is an INDEPENDENT BullMQ job. One failure does NOT block others.
- EventOutbox marked COMPLETED ONLY AFTER successful BullMQ enqueue.
- NO SellerContextGuard on any /notifications/* route.
- ALL notification DB queries filter by userId (INV-S6-18).
- Dedup key: notif:{userId}:{eventType}:{entityId} — NEVER use Date.now().
- OUTBOX_EVENT_NOTIFICATION_MAP is an extensible registry — NOT a switch/case.
- ONLY consume OrderStatusChanged for status events. NOT OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled.
- SupplierScoreUpdated notification: only when |delta| >= 5 points.
- Low stock SMS: max 1 per (productId, businessId) per 24 hours.
- Template rendering: safe string substitution ONLY. No eval(). Sanitize all variables.
- Phone/email are null-checked before delivery. null = skip + warn (NEVER throw).
- PushSubscription 410 Gone = delete subscription immediately (INV-S6-9).

HARDENING v1.1 RULES (INV-S6-21 through INV-S6-30) — DO NOT SKIP:
- CircuitBreakerService MUST wrap EVERY SmsChannel.send() and EmailChannel.send() call. (INV-S6-21)
  If isOpen('sms'/'email') returns true: return immediately — do NOT throw — do NOT enqueue retry.
  On Redis failure inside isOpen(): return false (assume CLOSED). NEVER assume OPEN on Redis failure.
- PushSubscription cap: MAX 10 active per user. Evict oldest on exceed. (INV-S6-22)
  Cap enforcement is INSIDE PushSubscriptionRepository.upsert() inside a $transaction.
- Email HTML: ALL template variables (title, body, CTA text) MUST be processed through htmlEscape() (INV-S6-23)
  BEFORE injection into HTML string. TemplateService.sanitize() is for SMS/plain-text ONLY.
  The separate htmlEscape() function handles the HTML context. These are NOT interchangeable.
- Notification list cursor MUST use notification `id` (CUID) — NOT createdAt. (INV-S6-24)
  OrderBy: { id: 'desc' }. Cursor filter: { id: { lt: query.cursor } }. Never { createdAt: { lt: ... } }.
- handleOrderCreated MUST set SEPARATE dedup keys for buyer and seller. (INV-S6-25)
  buyer: notif:{buyerId}:OrderCreated:{orderId}
  seller: notif:{sellerUserId}:OrderCreated:{orderId}
  Both set AFTER successful processing. Never share a single dedup key between buyer and seller.
- OutboxConsumerWorker.pollEventOutbox() MUST have isPolling guard. (INV-S6-26)
  private isPolling = false; — set true at entry, reset in finally block. NOT in catch block.
  If isPolling is true at cron entry: log OUTBOX_POLL_SKIPPED_OVERLAP and return immediately.
- validatePayload() MUST return { success: false } for unknown eventTypes. (INV-S6-27)
  NEVER return { success: true, data: payload } for an event with no registered schema.
  Unknown eventTypes are already caught at STEP 3 (no handler check) before validatePayload.
- TemplateSeedService upsert MUST use: update: { isActive: template.isActive } (INV-S6-28)
  Body fields (bodyHi, bodyEn, titleHi, titleEn) MUST NEVER be in the update object.
  Only isActive may be toggled by seed. Content changes require a deliberate migration.
- DELETE /notifications/push/unsubscribe MUST use ZodValidationPipe(PushUnsubscribeSchema). (INV-S6-29)
  Raw @Body() without validation allows null endpoint to reach the repository delete.
- notificationMonth MUST always be: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7) (INV-S6-30)
  Never use formatYearMonth(new Date()) or any locale/timezone-aware formatter.
  IST (UTC+5:30) at 00:01 would produce wrong month bucket without UTC anchoring.

IMPLEMENTATION SEQUENCE:
Phase 1 (DTOs) → Phase 2 (Domain Model) → Phase 3 (OutboxConsumer) →
Phase 4 (In-App) → Phase 5 (Email) → Phase 6 (SMS) → Phase 7 (Push) →
Phase 8 (Preferences) → Phase 9 (Templates) → Phase 10 (Retry/DLQ) →
Phase 11 (Center) → Phase 12 (Observability) → Phase 13 (Security) → Phase 14 (Validation)

BUILD AFTER EVERY PHASE:
pnpm --filter api build → must be 0 errors before proceeding to next phase.

HARDENING SELF-CHECK (run before marking any phase complete):

✅ CircuitBreakerService injected in SmsChannel and EmailChannel?

✅ NotificationRepository.findManyForUser() uses id cursor, not createdAt?
✅ order-created.handler.ts sets separate buyer AND seller dedup keys?
✅ OutboxConsumerWorker has isPolling field reset in finally block?
✅ validatePayload() returns { success: false } for unknown event types?
✅ TemplateSeedService update: only { isActive } — no body fields?
✅ NotificationController.unsubscribe() uses ZodValidationPipe(PushUnsubscribeSchema)?
✅ NotificationRepository.create() uses new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7) for notificationMonth?
```

### §28.2 Sprint 7 Admin Notification Pattern

> **AF-7 Audit Fix:** `sendDirect()` is referenced in §28.1 as "Exported from NotificationModule" and in §26.5 as `NotificationService.sendDirect()` but its method signature was NEVER defined anywhere in the implementation phases. This is corrected below. Sprint 6 implementation MUST include this method.

**`NotificationService.sendDirect()` — LOCKED Interface:**

```typescript
// In apps/api/src/modules/notification/services/notification.service.ts
// This method is the Sprint 7+ integration point — it MUST be exported from NotificationModule

/**
 * Directly triggers a notification outside the EventOutbox consumer path.
 * Used by AdminModule (Sprint 7) for KYC/suspension/system notifications.
 * Respects user notification preferences.
 * Always creates In-App. SMS/Email/Push per preference.
 *
 * @param userId     - Target user's ID (User.id — not Business.id)
 * @param templateName - Notification template name (must exist in NotificationTemplate table)
 * @param variables  - Template variable map ({ businessName: '...', orderNumber: '...', etc. })
 */
async sendDirect(
  userId: string,
  templateName: string,
  variables: Record<string, string>,
): Promise<void> {
  // 1. Resolve user contact
  const contact = await this.userContactService.getContact(userId);

  // 2. Determine channels from template definition
  const template = await this.notificationTemplateRepository.findByName(templateName);
  if (!template) {
    this.logger.error({ templateName, userId }, 'SEND_DIRECT_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND');
    return; // Graceful — never throw to caller
  }

  // 3. Determine event category from template type
  const category = this.getEventCategoryFromType(template.type);

  // 4. Delegate to createAndEnqueue — same preference + channel pipeline
  await this.createAndEnqueue({
    userId,
    contact,
    templateName,
    variables,
    entityId: userId,            // For dedup: userId as entityId (admin events are per-user)
    eventType: `Direct_${templateName}`,
    channels: template.channels.map(c => c.toLowerCase()) as ('sms' | 'email' | 'push' | 'inApp')[],
  });
}
```

**FOOTGUN-28-A:** Agent implements `NotificationService` but omits `sendDirect()`.
**Fix:** `sendDirect()` MUST be implemented in Phase 4 (In-App / NotificationService) alongside `createAndEnqueue()`. It is a public method on `NotificationService` that Sprint 7 will call. If missing, Sprint 7 `AdminModule` import will fail at compile time.

**FOOTGUN-28-B:** Agent makes `sendDirect()` bypass preference check.
**Fix:** `sendDirect()` delegates to `createAndEnqueue()` which performs preference check as its first operation (INV-S6-5). Do NOT call `createInAppNotification()` directly from `sendDirect()` — that would skip preference enforcement.

```typescript
// Sprint 7 usage (from AdminNotificationService inside AdminModule):
await this.notificationService.sendDirect(userId, 'KycApproved_SELLER_hi', {
  businessName: business.name,
});
// This creates In-App + SMS (per user preference) — Sprint 7 does NOT manage channels itself
```

### §28.3 Sprint 7 Must NOT

- Import `NotificationWorker` directly
- Write to `EventOutbox` with eventType `'KycApproved'` UNLESS it wants to trigger notification via outbox pattern
- Apply `SellerContextGuard` to admin notification routes (Admin has no businessId)
- Call `createInAppNotification()` or `createAndEnqueue()` directly — always use `sendDirect()`

## §30 HARDENING REPORT — v1.1

**Hardening Authority:** Enterprise Hardening Review Board + Security Review Committee + Scalability Review Committee + AI-Agent Implementation Safety Board
**Hardening Date:** Sprint 6 Pre-Implementation Phase
**Base Document Version:** v1.0 (Execution Lock)
**Hardened Document Version:** v1.1 (Hardened Execution Lock)

### §30.1 Hardening Mandate

This hardening was commissioned after Architecture Generation and before Implementation Authority issuance. The review board applied hostile analysis — attacking every assumption, challenging every design decision, and stress-testing the architecture against real-world failure scenarios at 1-to-1000 seller scale.

### §30.2 Attack Surfaces Identified and Closed

| # | Attack Surface | Severity | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SMS/Email retry storm on provider outage (no circuit breaker) | **HIGH** | INV-S6-21: `CircuitBreakerService` — 5 failures/60s → OPEN 120s |
| 2 | Push subscription amplification (unlimited endpoints per user) | **HIGH** | INV-S6-22: Hard cap 10/user, oldest evicted in `$transaction` |
| 3 | Email HTML injection via unescaped template variables | **HIGH** | INV-S6-23: `htmlEscape()` applied to all vars in `buildEmailHtml()` |
| 4 | `{{unsubscribeUrl}}` literal rendered in email body | **MEDIUM** | INV-S6-23 Note: Removed. Preferences API used for opt-out |
| 5 | `DELETE /push/unsubscribe` accepts unvalidated null endpoint | **MEDIUM** | INV-S6-29: `ZodValidationPipe(PushUnsubscribeSchema)` enforced |
| 6 | Seller receives duplicate notifications on outbox event replay | **MEDIUM** | INV-S6-25: Separate seller dedup key in all handlers |
| 7 | `validatePayload()` passes through unknown event types as valid | **MEDIUM** | INV-S6-27: Unknown schema returns `{ success: false }` |
| 8 | Cron overlap — concurrent batch processing under load | **MEDIUM** | INV-S6-26: `isPolling` guard in `finally` block |
| 9 | Template body silently overwritten on every app restart | **MEDIUM** | INV-S6-28: Seed `update: { isActive }` only, never body fields |
| 10 | `notificationMonth` timezone drift on IST/non-UTC servers | **LOW** | INV-S6-30: `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7)` always UTC |
| 11 | Cursor pagination breaks with millisecond-precision duplicates | **LOW** | INV-S6-24: CUID `id` cursor, not `createdAt` |

### §30.3 Architecture Strengthening Summary

| Component | Before Hardening | After Hardening |
|---|---|---|
| `SmsChannel` | Throws on error → BullMQ retries | Circuit breaker gates delivery. Open circuit = silent skip (no retry storm) |
| `EmailChannel` | Throws on error → BullMQ retries | Same circuit breaker pattern. HTML escape added |
| `PushSubscriptionRepository` | No cap — unbounded entries | Capped at 10/user in atomic `$transaction` |
| `OutboxConsumerWorker` | No cron overlap guard | `isPolling` in `finally` block prevents silent polling death |
| `order-created.handler` | Single buyer dedup key only | Separate buyer + seller dedup keys |
| `validatePayload()` | Unknown type passes through | Unknown type returns `{ success: false }` |
| `TemplateSeedService` | Overwrites body on every startup | `update: { isActive }` only — body is deploy-time data |
| `NotificationRepository` | `createdAt` cursor (non-unique) | CUID `id` cursor (monotonic, globally unique) |
| `NotificationRepository` | `formatYearMonth()` locale-aware | `toISOString().slice(0, 7)` UTC-anchored |
| `Redis Key Registry` | 6 keys documented | 10 keys documented + namespace rules + CB failure modes |
| `Module Structure` | No `CircuitBreakerService` | `circuit-breaker.service.ts` added to notification/services |

### §30.4 Scope Decisions Confirmed Unchanged

The following architecture decisions from `SPRINT_6_SCOPE_DECISIONS.md` were challenged and confirmed unchanged:

| Decision | Challenge | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Sprint 6 is pure EventOutbox consumer | "Should Sprint 6 write any outbox events?" | NO — INV-S6-1 unchanged |
| Push is best-effort (no DLQ) | "Should push have retry logic?" | NO — browser push is inherently unreliable |
| In-App is synchronous | "Should In-App be async BullMQ job?" | NO — In-App is last-resort channel. Must succeed even if BullMQ fails |
| No WhatsApp in Sprint 6 | "Should we add WhatsApp now?" | NO — INotificationChannel interface is extensible. Sprint 8+ decision |
| Preferences stored in DB (not Redis) | "Should Redis be the preference store?" | NO — Redis is cache only. DB is source of truth |

### §30.5 Remaining Accepted Risks (Non-Blocking)

| Risk | Accepted Reason | Future Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Template cache not hot-reloaded | MVP — template changes are infrequent | Sprint 8: admin template update API + hot reload |
| SMS `sendTransactional()` interface spec not in Sprint 1 | Sprint 1 `SmsService` interface must be extended | Implementer reads `sms.service.interface.ts` and adds method |
| WhatsApp channel union requires code change | Not additive when added | Sprint 8: refactor `INotificationChannel.name` to use enum or open string union |
| RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe header missing from emails | Low volume MVP — not required | Sprint 8: add `List-Unsubscribe` header to Resend emails |
| DLQ replay is manual (no admin UI) | Sprint 7 Admin tool planned | Sprint 7: `GET /admin/notifications/dlq` + replay endpoint |
| `Notification` DB has no `segment` field (OBS-S6-2) | Sprint 9 analytics join via metadata — manageable at current scale | Future migration: add `segment String?` to `Notification` model if Sprint 9 analytics demand direct query |

### §31.7 Scale & Operational Audit Summary

| Scenario | Audit Result |
|---|---|
| 1,000 sellers × 10 orders/day = 10,000 events/day | EventOutbox consumer: 50 events/5s batch = 600 events/min = 36,000 events/hr. Headroom: **3.6x buffer at 1K sellers.** ✅ |
| SMS provider outage (MSG91 down) | Circuit breaker opens after 5 failures. All subsequent SMS silently skipped for 120s. No retry storm. DLQ accumulates for manual replay. ✅ |
| OutboxConsumerWorker crash mid-batch | Events stay `PENDING`. On restart: Redis idempotency key prevents re-delivery of already-processed events. ✅ |
| 1 user, 11 devices subscribing push | Oldest subscription evicted in `$transaction`. Never exceeds 10. ✅ |
| Template content changed on production | Requires deliberate deploy — seed does NOT overwrite body on restart (INV-S6-28). ✅ |
| Notification table at 90 days, 10M rows | `notificationMonth` partition key + `idx_notif_user_read_date` — query scoped to user+isRead. Archive policy documented. ✅ |
| Two OutboxConsumerWorker instances | Redis lock `outbox-consumer-lock:{eventId}` prevents concurrent processing. Single in-memory `isPolling` per instance. Multi-instance safe. ✅ |

### §31.8 Non-Blocking Observations

These observations do NOT block implementation. They are documented for future sprint awareness.

**OBS-S6-1:** `PaymentReceived` payload has no `sellerId`. Sprint 6 correctly sends buyer-only payment confirmation. If a future sprint requires seller payment notification (e.g. "Buyer paid ₹50,000 — confirm dispatch"), a new `PaymentSettlementReady` event with `sellerId` must be added to the outbox, or `PaymentReceived` payload must be extended. Neither is a Sprint 6 action.

**OBS-S6-2:** `Notification` DB record has no `segment` field. Sprint 9 per-segment notification analytics will require joining `Notification.metadata.entityId` back to `EventOutbox.payload.segment`. This is manageable but adds a join. Future schema migration can add `segment String?` to `Notification` if analytics performance demands it. No Sprint 6 action required — `NotificationJob.segment` carries the value at metrics time.
